SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
S. 1, Special Branch 6/8/41 A
REPORT
Date August 5 1941. 41

Subject (in full) Shanghai Dockyards (British) - transient "tai-kung" strike

Made by D. I. Kao Yen Ken    Forwarded by D. S. I. Wilcox

With reference to the attached newspaper
translation in connection with a labour dispute in
the Shanghai Dockyards, 640 Yangtsepoo Road,
enquiries show that approximately 1,600 workers
of the Shanghai Dockyards went on a "go-slow"
strike at 6 a.m. July 29, to enforce a demand for
an increase in wages. The workers, however,
resumed work at 7.15 a.m. the same day, pending
negotiations with the management.

The workers are at present carrying on
their work as usual.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

6/5/41

A. C. (Special Branch).

Kao Yen-ken
D. I.

6 8 41

REPORT

Special Branch Station. File No. ____ Date May 7, 1941.

SUBJECT: Shanghai Dockyards - Chippers and painters on strike

Some 200 chippers and painters who were employed as casual workers by a number of contractors at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640 Yangtszepoo Road, on May 5, went on strike on the morning of May 6, 1941 to enforce a demand for an increase in their wages. The strikers were still out this morning.

The assistant manager Shanghai Dockyards Ltd. Mr. J.C. Amour was interviewed this morning by members of the Special Branch regarding the present situation of the strike. He stated that since all the workers on strike are casual labourers employed by contractors and not by the Shanghai Dockyards, the dispute would have to be settled by the contractors themselves. The contractors were later interviewed and the following particulars were ascertained :-

There are roughly 1,000 chippers and painters in Shanghai who are employed by various contractors as casual workers. Nearly all of these workers are natives of Kompo. Prior to March 24, 1941, these workers were paid $4 per diem. Since that date the workers have been granted an increase of $1 in their wages, i.e. $5 per diem. On the night of May 5, it was indicated by the chippers and painters that as a result of a discussion held by their labour union known as the "Chippers and Painters Union" (楗業工會) (address and particulars unknown), they intended to demand, due to high price of rice, a 40% increase in their pay, i.e. from $5 to $7, and that they would go on strike unless their demand was accepted. 特务处分处。档案号。____ 日期 1941年5月7日。

主题：上海船坞 - 铲锈工和油漆工罢工

受雇于杨树浦路640号上海船坞有限公司多家承包商的约200名作为临时工的铲锈工和油漆工，为强制要求增加工资，于1941年5月6日上午举行罢工。罢工者今晨仍未复工。

特务处成员今晨会见了上海船坞有限公司副经理 J.C. Amour 先生，了解罢工的当前情况。他表示，由于所有罢工工人均为承包商雇佣的临时工，而非上海船坞直接雇佣，因此纠纷必须由承包商自行解决。随后会见了几位承包商，查明了以下详情：

上海约有1,000名铲锈工和油漆工受雇于各承包商，作为临时工。这些工人几乎全是宁波人。在1941年3月24日之前，这些工人的日薪为4元。自该日起，工人工资增加了1元，即每日5元。5月5日晚，铲锈工和油漆工表示，经过其名为“铲漆业工会”（楗業工會）（地址及详情不详）的工会讨论后，他们打算因米价高涨而要求加薪40%，即从5元增至7元，并称除非要求被接受，否则将举行罢工。没有工人代表向承包商

The contractors of the Shanghai Dockyards,
11 in number, stated that they were reluctant to
entertain the demand of their workers for the following
two reasons: (1) the close proximity of the last
increase which was granted on March 24, 1941, and (2)
the high percentage of increase demanded. The
contractors added that if they accepted the demand,
they themselves would sustain a loss because the
contract for the work on which they are at present
engaged was agreed upon six weeks ago and cannot be
altered.

No mediation was offered due to absence of
any person to represent the workers. The contractors,
however, promised to inform the Special Branch of
future developments in the matter.

The situation is being watched.

Date March 1, 1941.

Subject 68 Sing Kong Li, Yangtszepoo Road.

Made by D.I. Kao Yen-ken, Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum. So, 6/6/44
A.I.

A ground-floor room of 68 Sing Kong Li,
Yangtszepoo Road was used as a meeting place for
members of the society of blacksmiths, employed in
the Shanghai Dockyards. This society was known as
the "Lao Chun Day" (老軍隊) (Group of Old Soldiers).
About three weeks ago, a dispute over
gambling occurred in the premises. A fight ensued
and furniture was smashed. Since this dispute, the
door of the room has been nailed and no further
meetings held.

Enquiries show that this society is a branch
of the "Shanghai Municipality Blacksmiths' Union,
Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, North Soochow
Road, which is registered with the "Bureau of
Social Affairs of the Shanghai City Government". It
has some 100 members, each of whom paid $0.60 a
month membership fee. The leader is Li Sih-yung
(李雪榮), a blacksmith in the employ of the
Shanghai Dockyards, his deputy is Wei Keng-ling
(魏根林), an ex-blacksmith.

It is also learned that some of its members
are concurrently members of the Ming Ziang (民祥)
Lien Nyi Society, Lane 129, 30 Ford Lane. This
latter society is an organization of followers of the
"Red Paung" who are known to be frequently engaged
to settle disputes by force. Wong Tieh-ming (王铁民)
and Chang Tsoo-ziang (張祖祥) are the leaders.

A.C. (Special Branch).
Kao Yen-ken

制作人 督察 高恩肯 (Kao Yen-ken), 转呈人 刑事侦缉督察 Tabrum。So, 1944年6月6日
助理督察。

杨树浦路新康里68号的一间底楼房间曾被用作受雇于上海船坞的铁匠社团成员的聚会场所。该社团被称为“老军队”（老軍隊）（老兵群体）。大约三周前，该场所发生了一起赌博纠纷。随后引发斗殴，家具被砸坏。自此次纠纷以来，该房间的门已被钉死，不再举行任何会议。

经查，该社团是位于北苏州路中国商会大楼的“上海市铁匠公会”的一个分支，该公会已在“上海市政府社会局”注册。它有约100名成员，每人每月缴纳0.60元会费。首领是李雪荣 (Li Sih-yung)，他是上海船坞雇佣的一名铁匠，其副手是魏根林 (Wei Keng-ling)，一名前铁匠。

还获悉，其部分成员同时也是民祥 (Ming Ziang) 联谊社的成员，该社位于福特路（今延安东路）129弄30号。后者是一个“红帮”追随者的组织，众所周知，他们经常受雇通过武力解决纠纷。王铁民 (Wong Tieh-ming) 和张祖祥 (Chang Tsoo-ziang) 是首领。

助理处长（特务处）。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. S. B. REGISTRY

S. I., Special Branch Station,
Date MAY 9, 19 40.

REPORT

Subject. Shanghai Dockyards - Labour situation.

Made by D.S.I. Logan, Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

（批：Re. 6/5/44 A.I.）

（左侧边栏手写批注：S.O.D O/c Yulin Rel）

Almost all workers, numbering 675, of the
Shanghai Dockyards, 640 Yangtszepoo Road, turned
up for work on May 8 and 9. Situation is normal
now.

With regard to the demands of the workers
for an increase of 20% in wages instead of 15%
granted and for the issue of pay for the period of
strike, the management refuses to enter into
negotiations with the workers. It is the opinion
of the management that after the labour situation
has been normal for some time, new representatives
of the workers may be appointed who can negotiate
a new labour agreement with the management and then
the management will be prepared to discuss the
workers' demands.

At 3 p.m. May 7, Mr. P.Y. Koo of the
Industrial Section, S.M.C., called at the dockyard
and discussed with the management the issue of
retiring gratuities to the remaining 40 discharged
workers. The main dispute is over the number of
years of services, in proportion to which retiring
gratuities are to be issued. A satisfactory
settlement of this matter has not yet been reached.

主题。上海船坞 - 劳工局势。

制作人 副督察长 Logan, 转呈人 督察 Crawford。

（批：Re. 1944年6月5日 A.I.）

（左侧边栏手写批注：S.O.D O/c Yulin Rel）

杨树浦路640号上海船坞的几乎所有工人，共计675人，于5月8日和9日均上班。目前局势正常。

关于工人要求加薪20%而非已批准的15%，以及发放罢工期间工资的要求，管理层拒绝与工人进行谈判。管理层认为，在劳工局势恢复正常一段时间后，可能会任命新的工人代表，与管理层协商新的劳工协议，届时管理层将准备讨论工人的要求。

5月7日下午3时，工部局工业科的顾佩玉 (P.Y. Koo) 先生来到船坞，与管理层讨论了向其余40名被解雇工人发放退休酬金的问题。主要争议在于服务年限，退休酬金将按比例据此发放。此事尚未达成令人满意的解决方案。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section I, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. 8941 P/Y
Date May 7th, 19 40.

Subject Shanghai Dockyards - workers resume work.

Made by D. S. I. Logan. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford. 18/6/5/44 D.I.

In answer to a notice of the management, posted
at 4 p.m. May 6th, some 500 out of a total of 675 workers
of the Shanghai Dockyards, 640 Yangtszepoo Road, resumed
work at a.m. May 7th. Some 100 more turned up later
and arrangements are being made for their returning to
work. It is expected that terms of working conditions
will be discussed later on May 7th.

With regard to the discharged workers, the
majority of the 210 concerned turned up and were paid
off on May 4th, but the minority still refuse to accept
the amount of retiring gratuities due to them pending
a settlement by the Industrial Section, S.M.C.

On May 2nd, Fitter No.206 Sze Wei Ming
( 施惠民 ), one of the leading agitators, who was
arrested by the Municipal Police on April 23rd in the
French Concession and released on April 27th , wrote
a letter to D.S.I. Kao, explaining that he was never
concerned in any illegal activities and had the intention
of always listening to Police instructions. In the
letter he finally announced that he swore to have nothing
more to do with the Shanghai Dockyards affairs or any
other organizations and would confine his attention to
his own professional business.

W. Logan
D. S. I.

主题 上海船坞 - 工人复工。

由 D. S. I. Logan 撰写。由 D. I. Crawford 转发。18/6/5/44 D.I.

为回应管理层于5月6日下午4时张贴的通知，位于杨树浦路640号的上海船坞（Shanghai Dockyards）总共675名工人中，约有500人于5月7日上午复工。随后又有约100人到场，正安排他们复工。预计将于5月7日稍后讨论工作条件条款。

关于被解雇的工人，涉及的210人中大多数已于5月4日到场并领取了遣散费，但少数人仍拒绝接受应得的退休酬金，等待工部局工业科作出裁决。

5月2日，钳工第206号施惠民（Sze Wei Ming），主要煽动者之一，曾于4月23日在法租界被工部局警务处逮捕，并于4月27日获释，他致信给副督察长高（D.S.I. Kao），解释称他从未参与任何非法活动，并有意始终听从警方指示。他在信中最后声明，他发誓不再过问上海船坞事务或任何其他组织的事宜，将只专注于自己的本职工作。

W. Logan

Subject. Shanghai Dockyards - labour situation.

Made by. D. S. I. Logan. Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

（批：Ver 6/5/44 A.I.）

The lockout of the Shanghai Dockyards
continues this morning, May 4th.

With regard to the arrangements made by
Mr. F.Y. Koo of the Industrial Section, S.M.C., for
the discharged men to be paid off at 10 a.m. May 3rd,
none of them turned up at the appointed time for the
money due to them. At 2.30 p.m. May 3rd, Mr. F.Y.
Koo approached some 100 workers gathered in the
temporary office of their union on Yangtszepoo Road
off Jansen Road. They put forward the following
fresh demands :-

1. That a yearly bonus of three days' wages be issued
to the discharged hands, in view of the fact that
they worked 3 months of the current year, and they
are entitled to ten days' holidays with pay per year.
2. That the photos of the discharged men be returned
to them.
3. That no receipt be signed by the discharged men when
they receive their retiring gratuities.
4. That the 41 men who should be paid retiring
gratuities according to the company's regulations
and re-employed when vacancies occur in the future,
be paid off in a similar way to those discharged
permanently.

（批：Ver 6/5/44 A.I.）

截至今天上午，5月4日，上海船坞的停工锁厂仍在继续。

关于工部局工业科顾方谊先生（Mr. F.Y. Koo）安排的于5月3日上午10时向被解雇工人发放薪金的事宜，无人按约定时间前来领取欠款。5月3日下午2时30分，顾方谊先生接触了聚集在杰森路（Jansen Road）旁杨树浦路工会临时办公室的大约100名工人。他们提出了以下新的要求：-

1. 鉴于被解雇工人在本年度已工作3个月，且每年享有10天带薪假期，应向被解雇工人发放相当于三天工资的年终奖金。
2. 将被解雇工人的照片归还给他们。
3. 被解雇工人在领取退休酬金时不得签署收据。
4. 根据公司规定应支付退休酬金并在未来出现空缺时重新雇用的41名工人，应以与永久解雇人员相同的方式结算薪金。

At 4.30 p.m. May 3, Mr. Koo referred the

dissatisfied and stated that unless the discharged
workmen call for their pay within 24 hours, no

Negotiations between the management and the
workers' delegates were continued in the Shanghai
Dockyards, Ltd., 640 Yangtsepoo Road, between 4 p.m.
and 5.15 p.m. May 1, with Mr. P.Y. Koo of the Industrial
Section, S.N.C., as the mediator. It was agreed that out
of the 231 undesirable workers, 21 will be reinstated, 169
will be paid according to company's regulations and re-
employed when vacancies should arise in future and the
remaining 41 will be discharged permanently. The 41
discharged workers will be granted a special retiring
gratuity equivalent to 25 days' wages in the event of
their services being less than 3 years and 50 days' wages
in the case of their services being between 3 and 6 years.
It was also arranged for the discharged men to call at
the dockyard for money due to them at 10 a.m. Friday,
May 3.

Mediation will be resumed at 3 p.m. May 3, when
working conditions for these workers to be taken back will
be discussed and thereafter a date will be fixed for the
resumption of operations by the dockyard.

With regard to the nine persons detained by
the Municipal Police for being concerned in the illegal
detention of a foreman in a lodging house in the French
Concession, they were released at 5 p.m. May 1, on the
instructions of D. C. (Special Branch). Five of the
nine persons who were not employees of the Shanghai
Dockyards, Ltd., were released only after a guarantor
named Chiu Yuan-foh (邱元福), Manager of the Doong Foong

5月1日下午4时至5时15分之间，在上海杨树浦路640号上海船坞有限公司（Shanghai Dockyards, Ltd.），在工部局工业科（原文误作 S.N.C.，应为 S.M.C.）顾方谊先生（Mr. P.Y. Koo，此处名字缩写与前文 F.Y. 不同，照实译出）的调解下，管理层与工人代表继续进行谈判。达成协议如下：在231名不受欢迎的工人中，21人将复职，16人将根据公司规定支付薪金，并在未来出现空缺时重新雇用，其余41人将被永久解雇。这41名被解雇工人将获得特别退休酬金，服务年限少于3年的相当于25天工资，服务年限在3至6年之间的相当于50天工资。还安排被解雇工人于5月3日星期五上午10时前往船坞领取欠款。

调解将于5月3日下午3时恢复，届时将讨论这些被召回工人的工作条件，此后将确定船坞恢复运营的日期。

关于因涉及在法租界一处寄宿公寓非法拘禁一名工头而被工部局警务处拘留的九人，他们根据特别支部副总监的指令，于5月1日下午5时获释。九人中有五人并非上海船坞有限公司的雇员，他们在名为邱元福（Chiu Yuan-foh）的担保人签署担保后才获释，邱元福系山东路32号同丰祥织布厂（Doong Foong Siang Weaving Factory）经理。

The five outsiders and fitter No. 206 (a leading agitator) were fingerprinted and found to have no previous Police record. Fitter No. 206 Sze Wei Ming was photographed for purpose of record in the event of his being concerned in further activities of an undesirable nature.

Before release, the five outsiders were further interrogated. All admitted being agents of the Ministry of Social Affairs, National Government, Chungking, whose duty is to seek labour information in Shanghai and meanwhile to make friends with the leading labour figures. They claimed that they had never received instructions to instigate labour agitation. In view of the Japanese influence in Shanghai, they kept their identity as secret as possible. All of them are followers of Chow Hsueh-siang (周學湘), a committee member of the now defunct Kuomintang-sponsored General Labour Union, who had, prior to the hostilities, influence over labour matters north of the Soochow Creek. They have no office and their immediate superior is one Zung Zung-en, who keeps his movements secret. All reports, etc., were forwarded through Tu Yueh-sung's residence, 216 Rue Wagner.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Woo Mang Ling (胡夢麟)
native of ............................................................taken by me D.S.I. Logan
                                                                 D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken
                                                                 C.D.C. 30
at Police Hdqrs. on the May 1, 1940, and interpreted by Clerk Hsu Ta Yung.

My name is Woo Mang Ling. I was arrested at Room
63 Tsung Kiang No.3 Lodging House, Rue Palikao, French
Concession, on April 23, whilst I was collecting
information from workers of the Shanghai Dockyards in
connection with their strike situation.
A notebook of mine was found in my possession
which contains names and addresses of 6 workers of the
Wuchow Road P.W.D. Depot and with reference thereto, I
beg to state as follows :-
Towards the end of February, 1940, acting on
instructions to enlist intelligence agents given me by
one Zung Zung En (陳任安), an agent of the Social
Affairs Bureau of the Central Government to promote the
People's Movement in Shanghai who is my superior officer
and who has a communication address at Mr. Tu Yueh Sung's
(杜月笙) residence on Rue Wagner, French Concession,
I wrote to my friend Cheu Kya Shing (鄒家興), a
coolie employed at the East Asia Cigarette Factory,
Baikal Road, and residing at 61 Zung Zer Li, Baikal Road,
stating that I wished to talk with him on important
matters.
At about 2 p.m., March 3, 1940, I met Cheu Kya
Shing as appointed, at the offices of San Tai Company
(三德), Room 321, 540 Ningpo Road, when I
requested him to introduce some intelligence agents to
me.
During the forenoon of March 10, 1940, I booked

以下为胡梦麟（Woo Mang Ling）的供词，籍贯 ____，由副督察长洛根（D.S.I. Logan）、副督察长高延肯（D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken）及刑事侦缉处第30组（C.D.C. 30）于1940年5月1日在警察总局录取，由书记员徐达庸翻译。

我叫胡梦麟。我于4月23日在法租界贝勒路（Rue Palikao）宗江第三客栈63号房间被捕，当时我正在从上海船坞的工人那里收集有关他们罢工情况的信息。
在我身上发现了一本笔记本，其中记录了梧州路工务局仓库6名工人的姓名和地址，就此我陈述如下：
1940年2月底，我奉中央政府社会事务局驻上海负责民众运动专员陈任安（Zung Zung En）之命招募情报人员，他是我的上级，其通讯地址为法租界华格纳路（Rue Wagner，现名淮海中路）杜月笙先生寓所。我写信给我的朋友邹家兴（Cheu Kya Shing），他是百克尔路（Baikal Road，现名惠民路）东亚卷烟厂的苦力，住在百克尔路宗泽里61号，称我有要事想与他商谈。
1940年3月3日下午2时许，我按约定在三德公司（San Tai Company）办公室与邹家兴会面，地址为宁波路540号321室，当时我请他向我介绍一些情报人员。

Date May 1, 19 40.

Subject Shanghai Dockyards - labour situation.

Made by. D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford 6/5/44

between 10 a.m. and 12 noon and between
3 p.m. and 5 p.m. on April 30, negotiations
were carried on between the management and the
workers' foremen in the Shanghai Dockyards, 640
Yangtsepoo Road, with Mr. P.Y. Koo, Industrial
Section, Shanghai Municipal Council, as mediator.
Problems relating to the discharge of 300 workers
were discussed and an agreement was reached on
the following basis :-

1. 10% of the 300 discharged workers will
be reinstated.

2. 30% will be paid off according to the
company's regulations (between 1 year's
and 3 years' service - a retiring
gratuity equivalent to 25 days' pay and
between 3 and 6 years' - 35 days' pay).
The discharged workers will be given
preference when future vacancies occur.

3. 60% will be paid off for good according
to the following scale :-
a) less than 3 years' service - 25 days' pay
b) more than 3 years' service - 50 days' pay
c) more than 6 years' service - 75 days' pay

A further meeting was arranged for 3 p.m. May 1,
when the classification of the 300 workers according
to the above-mentioned percentage will be decided
upon.

It is learned that the management has
decided to settle the discharge problem first,
and after paying off the discharged hands on
either Thursday or Friday, will discuss terms

制作人：副督察长洛根 转呈人：督察长克劳福德 1944年5月6日

4月30日上午10时至12时以及下午3时至5时之间，在上海船坞（杨树浦路640号），资方与工人领班进行了谈判，由上海公共租界工部局工业科科长顾某（P.Y. Koo）担任调解人。会议讨论了关于解雇300名工人的问题，并达成如下协议基础：

1. 被解雇的300名工人中，10%将复职。

2. 30%将根据公司规定予以遣散（服务满1年至3年者，退休金相当于25天工资；服务满3年至6年者，相当于35天工资）。将来出现空缺时，被解雇工人将享有优先录用权。

3. 60%将按以下标准彻底遣散：
a) 服务不满3年者 - 25天工资
b) 服务超过3年者 - 50天工资
c) 服务超过6年者 - 75天工资

另定于5月1日下午3时召开进一步会议，届时将根据上述百分比确定这300名工人的分类。

据悉，资方决定先解决解雇问题，并在周四或周五支付被解雇工人的款项后，再讨论

（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE File No. REGISTRY 8941 E/1 S. B. D. 314/61, L）
Date April 30th, 1940.
Subject. Shanghai Dockyards - Arrest of 20 strike leaders and present labour situation.
Made by. D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by D. I. Crawford. （批：Se 6/5/44 A.I.）

Forwarded herewith is a list of documents seized from Room 63 and 78, Tsung Kiang Lodging House No.3, 63 Rue Palikao, at 11 a.m. April 23rd.

The 20 prisoners have been interrogated. Of these 20, 15 are workers of the Shanghai Dockyards, while the remaining five claimed to be agents of the "Resident Deputy in charge of the People's Movement in Shanghai of the Ministry of Social Affairs of the Central Government, Chungking" seeking for information regarding the labour dispute in the Shanghai Dockyards. When questioned, the foreman of the International Dockyards stated that he was brought to Shanghai from lootung by a worker No.116 Yih Ching Hwa ( 葉錦華 ) and that the latter refused him permission to leave the lodging house above mentioned. Of the 14 workers, only two are known to be leaders, namely, Sze Wei Ming ( 施惠民 ) and Zung Ping Kong ( 陳炳康 ), while the remaining 12 stated that they visited the rooms with a view to obtaining information as to when they could resume work. Statements of the foreman, two leaders and five outsiders have been taken and are attached hereto.

Between 2.30 p.m. and 3 p.m. April 26th, some 350 workers of the Shanghai Dockyards held a meeting on a piece of vacant ground on Yangtszepoo Road off Jansen Road. Fitter No.116 presided over

制作人：副督察长洛根 转呈人：督察长克劳福德。（批注：Se 1944年5月6日 A.I.）

随函附上4月23日上午11时从贝勒路63号宗江第三客栈63号和78号房间搜获的文件清单。

20名囚犯已受审问。在这20人中，15人是上海船坞的工人，其余5人声称是“重庆中央政府社会事务部驻上海负责民众运动常驻副专员”的特工，正在寻求有关上海船坞劳资纠纷的信息。在接受讯问时，国际船坞的一名领班称，他是由116号工人叶锦华（Yih Ching Hwa）从罗通（lootung，音译）带到上海的，后者拒绝允许他离开上述客栈。在这14名工人中，只有两人已知是领袖，即施惠民（Sze Wei Ming）和陈炳康（Zung Ping Kong），其余12人表示，他们访问这些房间是为了获取何时可以复工的信息。该领班、两名领袖和五名外来人员的供词已录取并附后。

4月26日下午2时30分至3时之间，约350名上海船坞工人在杨树浦路近詹森路（Jansen Road，现名宁国路）的一块空地上举行集会。钳工116号主持了

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Zung Ping Kong (陳 炳 康)
native of Ningpo, Chekiang taken by me D.S.I. Logan
D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken
C.D.C. 50
at Police Hdqrs. on the April 26, 1940 and interpreted by

My name is Zung Ping Kong. I am 39 years of age,
a native of Ningpo, married, and residing at No. 3 Tai
Oen Li (泰 安 里), North Shanse Road.
I joined the old factory of the Shanghai Dockyards,
640 Yangtszepoo Road, as an apprentice in 1917 and was
transferred to the new factory in 1932.
On March 14, 1940, about 50 coolies went on
strike to enforce demands for changes in shifts and a
rice allowance. On March 15, 1940, I and ten other
representatives engaged Room 67, San Bang (三 朋)
Lodging House, Rue Palikao, for the purpose of discussing
matters relating to negotiations with the management.
Up to April 3, no settlement was reached.
Kao Pah Shi (高 伯 希), Chief of the Organization
Department of the Eastern District Branch of the Chinese
Labourers' Welfare Association (127 Rangoon Road), often
visited us in the lodging house to collect information
regarding the strike and to persuade us to proceed to the
Association. In order to avoid him, we, on April 4, 1940,
removed to Room 78, Tsung Kiang No. 3 Lodging House, Rue
Palikao, where we continued discussions re negotiations
with the management. As too many strikers came to enquire
about the result of negotiations, we engaged another
room, No. 63, in the same lodging house. Some time
afterwards, we requested Mr. Yuan Lu Tung, Chinese
Councillor of Shanghai Municipal Council, to mediate in
the dispute but this was rejected by the management.

以下是陈炳康（Zung Ping Kong）的供词，浙江宁波人，由我副督察 Logan、副督察高延肯（Kao Yen Ken）、刑事侦缉处第50组于1940年4月26日在警察总局录取，并由______翻译

我叫陈炳康（Zung Ping Kong）。今年39岁，宁波人，已婚，居住在北山西路泰安里3号。
我于1917年进入位于杨树浦路640号的上海船坞旧厂当学徒，并于1932年转入新厂。
1940年3月14日，约50名苦力罢工，以强制要求改变轮班制度和发放米贴。1940年3月15日，我和其他十名代表在帕利考路三朋旅馆67室租房，目的是讨论与管理层谈判的相关事宜。
截至4月3日，未达成和解。
中国劳工福利协会东区分会（兰格路127号）组织部主任高伯希（Kao Pah Shi）经常到旅馆拜访我们，收集有关罢工的信息，并劝我们去该协会。为了避开他，我们于1940年4月4日搬至帕利考路宗江3号旅馆78室，在那里继续讨论与管理层的谈判事宜。由于太多罢工工人来询问谈判结果，我们在同一家旅馆又租了63室。不久之后，我们请求上海公共租界工部局华董袁履东先生调解纠纷，但被管理层拒绝。

At 8 p.m., April 22, worker No. 116 Yih Ching Hwa (葉錦華) of the Dockyards, and worker No. 2 Zee Chi Kung (徐季根) of the International Dock in Pootung, called at the lodging house. I do not know the reason of their visit. I asked Yih about the result of the negotiations with the management and he replied that a further meeting would be held with the management the following day. I returned home at about 10 p.m. At 9 a.m., the following day, I went to Room 63 of the Tsung Kiang Lodging House, where I was arrested by the Police at 10.30 a.m. I know nothing about the case of detention which was committed by worker No. 116 named Yih Ching Hwa.

During the strike in November, 1939, some 400 workers joined the Chinese Labourers' Welfare Association, and each of them paid an entrance fee of $1.00. As the association did nothing in that strike, we made no contact with it in connection with the present strike.

At the beginning of March, 1940, copies of a proclamation of the "Bureau of Social Affairs" urging workers to register with the Bureau's branch office in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, were posted in Yangtszepoo. Some 100 workers employed in different departments of the Shanghai Dockyards, effected registration; I did not do so. The registered workers have had nothing to do with the Bureau since the registration.

Signed & Thumb Printed:
Zung Ping Kong.

1940年4月22日晚8时，船坞第116号工人叶锦华（Yih Ching Hwa）和浦东国际码头第2号工人徐季根（Zee Chi Kung）来到旅馆。我不知道他们来访的原因。我问叶锦华与管理层谈判的结果，他回答说第二天将与管理层举行进一步会议。我于当晚10点左右回家。次日上午9时，我前往宗江旅馆63室，上午10时30分被警察逮捕。我对第116号工人叶锦华所犯的拘留案件一无所知。

在1939年11月的罢工期间，约400名工人加入了中国劳工福利协会，每人缴纳入会费1.00元。由于该协会在那次罢工中无所作为，我们在本次罢工中未与其联系。

1940年3月初，杨树浦张贴了“社会局”的公告副本，敦促工人在华商总会大楼的社会局分局登记。上海船坞各部门约有100名工人进行了登记；我没有登记。登记后的工人与社会局再无往来。

签名并按指印：
陈炳康（Zung Ping Kong）。

My name is Sz Wei Ming (施惠民). I am 26 years of age, a native of Footung, married, and residing at No.20 Yang Kao Zah, Footung.

In July, 1938, I obtained employment as worker No. 206 attached to the Dock Side Machine Department of the Shanghai Dockyards, 640 Yangtsepoo Road. Up to March, 1940, I was suspended for want of work on two occasions, each for a period of about one month.

On March 13, 1940, the workers declared a strike owing to violation of the working agreement on the part of the management. I was appointed one of the eleven representatives who organized the Shanghai Dockyards Workers' Union in a country house at Tsoo Ka Za (左家宅), Yangtsepoo.

To facilitate communications, we on the 16th, March engaged rooms 66 and 76 in the San Bang (三朋) Lodging House, Rue Palikao, French Concession. Zung Ping Kong (陳炳康), Yih Ching Hwa (葉錦華) and I Myself always remained in the lodging house to arrange matters relating to negotiations and to meet mediators. The other eight representatives took charge of the union in Yangtsepoo, and controlled the activities of the workers etc. A communications group undertook the transfer of messages.

On April 4, we removed to rooms 78 & 63 in the Tsung Kiang (春江) No. 3 Lodging House, Rue Palikao, because the two rooms in the San Bang Lodging House were found to be too small for the many callers and also

我叫施惠民（Sz Wei Ming）。今年26岁，浦东人，已婚，居住于浦东杨高扎20号。

1938年7月，我在位于杨树浦路640号的上海船坞岸边机器部受雇为第206号工人。截至1940年3月，我因缺乏工作两次被停职，每次为期约一个月。

1940年3月13日，由于管理层违反工作协议，工人宣布罢工。我被任命为十一名代表之一，他们在杨树浦左家宅的一所乡间别墅组织了上海船坞工人联合会。

为了方便联络，我们于3月16日在法租界帕利考路三朋旅馆租了66和76室。陈炳康（Zung Ping Kong）、叶锦华（Yih Ching Hwa）和我本人一直留在旅馆，安排谈判相关事宜并会见调解人。其他八名代表负责杨树浦的工会事务，并控制工人的活动等。一个联络小组负责传递消息。

4月4日，我们搬至帕利考路宗江（Tsung Kiang）3号旅馆的78和63室，因为三朋旅馆的两个房间被发现太小，无法容纳众多访客，而且

because members of the Chinese Labourers' Welfare

One day in April, I cannot remember the date,
I felt that the dispute could hardly be settled and
therefore I resigned from the post of representative and
returned to my home in Pootung. On the day after my
arrival at Pootung, I received a letter, jointly signed
by the ten representatives, insisting upon my return on
the ground that my resignation would give the management
an impression that there was a split among the workers'
organization. I did as requested. At 8 p.m., April 22,
Yih Ching Hwa (葉錦華), accompanied by Zee Chi Kung
(余紀根), a representative of the workers of the
International Dock, Pootung and Zee's friend named Koo
(顧 ), visited Room 78 of the Tsung Kiang Lodging House.
At that time there were more than 10 workers in the room.
Yih reported on the negotiations conducted in the
International Dock and expressed the opinion that capital
and labour could reach an agreement. The workers in the
room felt relieved upon hearing his report, and left one
after another. Yih, Zee, Koo (Zee's friend) and myself
remained overnight in Room 78. Yih left for Pootung
about 8 a.m., the following day. I deny the allegation at
that I detained Zee Chi Kung.

Signed & Thumb-printed,
Sz Wei Ming.

因为中国劳工福利会（日本资助）的成员为了进行煽动活动而访问了这些房间。

四月中的某一天，具体日期我已记不清，我觉得这场纠纷很难解决，因此我辞去了代表职务，回到了我在浦东的家中。在我到达浦东的第二天，我收到了一封由十位代表联合签署的信，坚持要求我回去，理由是我的辞职会给管理层造成工人组织内部出现分裂的印象。我照他们的要求做了。4月22日晚上8点，叶锦华（Yih Ching Hwa） accompanied by 余纪根（Zee Chi Kung，浦东国际码头工人代表）以及余的一位姓顾（Koo）的朋友，访问了崇江旅馆78号房间。当时房间里有十多名工人。叶汇报了在国际码头进行的谈判情况，并表示资方和劳方可以达成协议。房间里的工人听到他的汇报后感到宽慰，便陆续离开。叶、余、顾（余的朋友）和我本人在78号房间过夜。叶在第二天早上8点左右前往浦东。我否认当时我扣留了余纪根的说法。

签名并按手印，
施惠民（Sz Wei Ming）。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Zee Chi Keng ( 徐 池 根 )
native of Ningpo, Chekiang, taken by me D.S.I. Logan
D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken
C.D.C. 30
at Police Hdqrs., on the April 25, 1940, translated and interpreted by Clerk Tan Hwueh Hua.

My name is Zee Chi Keng ( 徐 池 根 ), aged 48, a native of Ningpo, married, residing in the quarters of the International Dock in Pootung.

At about 6 p.m. on April 22, 1940, while I was in the International Dock in Pootung, one named Yeh Ching Hwa ( 葉 錦 華 ), who is worker No. 116 of the Shanghai Dockyards, asked me to accompany him to the Tsung Kiang 3rd Lodginghouse ( 崇 江 三 號 旅 館 ), on Rue Palikao.

I refused him at first but later I gave my consent as I was under the apprehension that he might do something unfavourable to me. I accompanied him to Room No. 78 Tsung Kiang 3rd Lodginghouse on Rue Palikao.

I observed some 30 persons in the room, who reproached me for breaking the strike.

I was compelled to stay overnight in the company of Worker No. 116 named Yeh Ching Hwa and four others ( names unknown).

At 7 a.m. on April 23, I told Yeh Ching Hwa that I wished to go home. He stated that I was not allowed to go until his return at 4 p.m. when he would receive instructions which would decide whether I would be allowed to go home.

Subsequently some 10 workers of the Shanghai Dockyards arrived in the Room.

At 10.30 a.m. I was arrested by the Police.

Signed and Thumb Printed:
Zee Chi Keng.

以下系由本人副督察长洛根（D.S.I. Logan）、副督察长高延肯（D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken）、C.D.C. 30 于1940年4月25日在警察总局对籍贯为浙江宁波的徐池根（Zee Chi Keng）所作的供词记录，并由职员谭学华（Tan Hwueh Hua）翻译和口译。

我叫徐池根（Zee Chi Keng），48岁，浙江宁波人，已婚，居住在浦东国际码头的宿舍。

1940年4月22日下午6点左右，当我在浦东国际码头时，上海船厂的第116号工人叶锦华（Yeh Ching Hwa）请我陪他去帕科路（Rue Palikao，今四平路）的崇江三号旅馆（Tsung Kiang 3rd Lodginghouse）。

起初我拒绝了他，但后来因为我担心他可能会做出对我不利的事情，所以我同意了。我陪他去了帕科路崇江三号旅馆的78号房间。

我看到房间里大约有30个人，他们指责我破坏罢工。

我被迫与第116号工人叶锦华及其他四人（姓名不详）一起过夜。

4月23日早上7点，我告诉叶锦华我想回家。他说在我得到允许之前不能走，要等到他下午4点回来，届时他会接到指示，决定我是否被允许回家。

随后，大约十名上海船厂的工人来到了房间。

上午10点30分，我被警察逮捕。

签名并按手印：
徐池根。

My name is Wu Mang Ling, aged 29, a native of
Ningpo, single, residing at No. 17, Tso Lan Tsung
( 竹蘭邨 ), Poo Tung Road ( 蒲東路 ), French
Concession.

During 1928, I was a committee-man of the Hwa
Zung Tobacco Factory Workers' Union, Wayside Road and
in 1932 I was concurrently a member of the Executive
Committee of the Shanghai Municipality General Labour
Union.

In July, 1937, I was the Chief of the General
Affairs Department of the Shanghai Labour Circles National
Salvation Association. Following the outbreak of
hostilities on August 13, 1937, I joined the Shanghai
Emergency Relief Committee, having been appointed to the
position of a secretary of the Repatriation Section of
the Committee. Following the withdrawal of the Chinese
National Army from Shanghai Area in 1937, I proceeded
to the Cheng Hai District, near Ningpo, where I served
in the General Labour Union in the capacity of Director
of Readjustment.

In July, 1938, I proceeded to Yu Yao District
(Chekiang), where I served in the capacity of Director
of People's Movement of the Salf District General Labour
Union of the Yu Yao District.

I returned to Shanghai in August, 1939, taking up
residence in the house of my relative named Lee on the
3rd floor of premises No. 62, Loh An Fong, Avenue Joffre,

我叫胡梦麟，29岁，浙江宁波人，未婚，居住在法租界蒲东路（Poo Tung Road）竹兰邨（Tso Lan Tsung）17号。

1928年期间，我是韦司德路（Wayside Road，今余姚路）华成烟草厂工人委员会的委员，1932年我兼任上海市总工会执行委员会委员。

1937年7月，我担任上海各界救亡协会总务部主任。1937年8月13日战事爆发后，我加入了上海紧急救济委员会，被任命为该委员会遣送组秘书。1937年中国国民军队从上海地区撤退后，我前往宁波附近的镇海区，在那里我在总工会任职，担任调整委员会主任。

1938年7月，我前往浙江余姚区，在那里我担任余姚区萨尔弗区（Salf District，原文如此，可能指特定区域或拼写错误）总工会民众运动主任。

我于1939年8月回到上海，住在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre，今淮海中路）罗安坊（Loh An Fong）62号三楼我的亲戚李（Lee）姓人家中，

我一直住到12月18日，随后我在法租界蒲东路竹兰邨17号租了一所房子自住。

自1939年8月回到上海以来，我一直受雇担任“重庆中央政府社会部驻沪民众运动特派员办事处”的秘书。

My name is Sz Chi Chong ( 施其昌 ). I am 31 years
of age, a native of Yu Yao ( 餘姚 ), Chekiang, and married.
I am residing at No. 11, Chien Nyih Lee, Rue Frelupt, French
Concession.

Prior to the present Sino-Japanese hostilities, I
was employed in the Chien Dah Rice Hong at Ningpo. I left
the position and came to Shanghai during February, 1940.
Through the recommednation of Tsau Sz Ming ( 曹治民 ), I
obtained employment as Investigator of the Shanghai
Inspectorate Office of the Ministry of Social Affairs of
the Central Government, Chunking at a monthly salary of $30.
I do not know the office address but I used to send my
reports to No. 120 Pao Yui Li ( 寶裕里 ) Avenue Edward VII,
from where the reports are collected by somebody.

At the beginning of April, I went to Room 78, Tsung
Kiang No. 3 Lodging House, Rue Palikao, for the purpose of
getting information regarding the strike at the Shanghai
Dockyards. As I know Zung Ping Kong ( 陳炳康 ), a worker
of the dockyards, he asked me to copy documents and to pay
accounts on his behalf. From the beginning of April to
April 23, I paid five or six visits to the lodging house.

Sz Chi Chong.

我叫施其昌（Sz Chi Chong）。我31岁，浙江余姚人，已婚。我居住在法租界弗雷吕普路（Rue Frelupt，今复兴中路）建义里（Chien Nyih Lee）11号。

在目前的中日敌对行动之前，我在宁波的谦达米行（Chien Dah Rice Hong）工作。1940年2月，我离职来到上海。通过曹治民（Tsau Sz Ming）的介绍，我获得了重庆中央政府社会部上海视察员办事处调查员的职位，月薪30元。我不知道办公地址，但我通常将报告发送到爱德华七世路（Avenue Edward VII，今金陵东路）宝裕里（Pao Yui Li）120号，由某人从那里收取报告。

四月初，我前往帕科路（Rue Palikao）崇江三号旅馆78号房间，目的是获取有关上海船厂罢工的信息。因为我认识船厂工人陈炳康（Zung Ping Kong），他让我代为抄写文件并支付账目。从四月初到4月23日，我去过该旅馆五六次。4月23日上午10点，我在那里被捕。

（签名） ____
施其昌。
按手印。

The following is the statement of Zao Tee Ming ( 曹 子 明 )

and interpreted by Tan Hsueh Hua

My name is Zao Tee Ming, aged 30, a native of
Shanghai, married, residing at No.9, Sing Jao Zah,
Lunghwa.

In 1930, I was the principal of the Hwa Zung
Tobacco Factory Workers' Children's Evening School, 276
Wayside Road and concurrently secretary of the 4th District
Rolled Tobacco Workers' Union.

Following the outbreak of the local hostilities
in August 1937, I served in the capacity of secretary in
the Repatriation Section of the Shanghai Emergency Relief
Committee, 1454 Avenue Edward VII. Following the with-
drawal of the Chinese army at the end of 1937, I proceeded
to Hankow, where I enrolled in the Political Training
Course of the Officers' Training Corps. After graduation
from the Corps, I was detailed to Yu Yao, Chekiang, where
I served in the capacity of Political Instructor with the
rank of Major in the 1st column of the 6th Branch Company
of the People's Anti-Enemy (Japanese) and Defence Corps.

In May, 1939, I served in the Yu Yao District
Party Headquarters and subsequently served in the Yu Yao
Government in the capacity of a secretary.

In February 1940, I returned to Shanghai and
joined the office of the Resident Deputy in charge of
People's Movement in Shanghai of the Ministry of Social
Affairs of the Central Government.

At 7 a.m. on April 23rd, 1940, I left Lunghwa
and proceeded to call on ZUNG PING KONG ( 陳炳康 ) at
page_data.zh:

我叫曹子明，30岁，上海人，已婚，居住在龙华辛家宅（Sing Jao Zah）9号。

1930年，我是韦司德路（Wayside Road）276号华成烟草厂工人夜校的校长，并兼任第四区卷烟工人联合会秘书。

1937年8月局部战事爆发后，我在爱德华七世路1454号上海紧急救济委员会遣送组担任秘书。1937年底中国军队撤退后，我前往汉口，在那里参加了军官训练团的政治训练班。从训练团毕业后，我被派往浙江余姚，在那里我在人民抗敌（日本）自卫总队第六支队第一大队担任政治指导员，军衔少校。

1939年5月，我在余姚区党部任职，随后在余姚县政府担任秘书。

1940年2月，我回到上海，加入了中央政府社会部驻沪民众运动特派员办事处。

1940年4月23日早上7点，我离开龙华，前往北山西路泰安里3号拜访陈炳康（ZUNG PING KONG），

My name is Loh Ser Tseng ( 陸守正 ), alias Loh
Yung Ling ( 陸榮林 ), aged 53, a native of Yu Yao,
Chekiang, single-widower, residing in the room above the
kitchen, at No. 28, Jen Teh Fong, Dalny Road, off Ward
Road.

Before the outbreak of hostilities, I was employed
in the Ginsen Trade Guild in Nantao. In the course of
the local hostilities I served in the Southern District
War Time Citizens' Service Corps. Following the withdrawal
of the Chinese National Army from Shanghai Area, I took
refuge in the Foreign Settlement for about 10 days, after
my arrival in Yu Yao, I served in the Salt Trade Guild
and concurrently served as inspector in the office of
Salt District Anti-Enemy (Japanese?) and Defence
Association. I resigned from these positions in September,
1939, owing to a difference of opinion with the Chief of
the Guild. Since then I remained unemployed in my native
home until March, 1940 when I arrived in Shanghai in quest
of employment.

During April, 1940, I joined the office of the
Resident Deputy in Charge of People's Movement in Shanghai
of the Ministry of Social Affairs of the Central Government,
Chungking, through the introduction of one Zao Tse Ming
( 曹澤民 ), receiving a monthly salary of $46.00.
I have never visited the office in question, therefore
I do not know the exact location of the office. I
understand that this office is mainly concerned in the

本人姓名陆守正，别名陆荣林（Loh Yung Ling），现年53岁，浙江余姚人，鳏夫，居住于华德路大连路口仁德坊28号厨房楼上房间。

战事爆发前，本人在南市参业公会任职。在当地战事期间，本人服务于南区战时市民服务团。中国国军撤离上海地区后，本人避入租界约十天，抵达余姚后，本人在盐业公会任职，并兼任盐区抗敌（日本？）自卫会办事处视察员。1939年9月，因与公会主任意见不合，本人辞去上述职务。此后本人在家乡失业，直至1940年3月抵沪谋职。

My name is Hsu Chih Sung, aged 42, married, a
native of Yue Yao, residing at 102 Zung Shing Fang ( 順興坊 ),
Ward Road.

In 1932 I came to Shanghai and lived at the above
address for about one year without employment. From 1933
I was employed as a shop assistant for more than 2 years in
Wei Tai Chong ( 魏泰昌 ) Cigarettes & Money Exchange Shop,
at the mouth of Yoeh Hwa Fang ( 月華坊 ), Ward Road.

In June 1935 I served as a member of the general
affairs department of the Hwa Zung ( 華成 ) Primary School.
After the outbreak of the current hostilities I lost my job.
In April 1938 I was employed as a worker in the Accountant
Room of the China Import & Export Lumber Company at Yang-
tszepoo Road with a salary of $30.00 per mensem and am
still in this position.

In November 1939, being introduced by my cousin
Chow Hsueh Siang ( 周學湘 ), I served as an investigator
of the Shanghai Inspectorate Office of the Ministry of
Social Affairs of the Central Government, Chungking with
a salary of more than $10.00 per mensem. At 7 a.m.
April 23rd, 1940 I recieved a telephone call from Woo Mong
Ling ( 胡夢麟 ) in Room 78 Tsung Kiang No.3 Hotel, Rue
Palikao, telling me to see him there at 9.30 a.m. that date.
When I arrived, Woo was not in that room. Led by worker
No.179 Chen Chih Keng ( 陳志根 ) of the Shanghai Dockyards
to Room 63, I met Woo Mong Ling who told me to accompany

Subject. Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., - Strike. Raid on Union Office -
20 Arrests

Made by. D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford （批：6/5/44 G-J）

At 10.30 a.m. 23.4.40, Mr. Bonnyman, Manager
of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., telephoned to
say that he was in possession of information
to the effect that the chief leaders of the
strikers had an office at Room 78 of the No. 3
Chuen Kiang (春江) lodging House, 33 Rue Palikao,
French Concession and that they had ordered the
No. 2 Fitter of the International Dock, Pootung,
to come to the aforesaid room on the morning of
23.4.40 under pain of threats of violence in order
to discuss the situation at the International Dock
where the whole complement of workers have gone
back to work. Mr. Bonnyman stated that he believed
that the strikers intended to attempt further
intimidation of the International Dock, Pootung,
workers, in order to compel them to cease work
again and so assist them in effecting a settlement
of their strike in the Yangtsepool Dock. It was
urgently requested by Mr. Bonnyman that the Police
should raid the Union Office mentioned in order
to avert further intimidation of the International
Dock workers.

With the assistance of the French Police,
attached to Post Joffre, D.S.I. Logan and C.D.S.
281 (Special Branch) visited Rooms 78 and 63 of the

事由：上海船坞有限公司——罢工。突袭工会办事处——逮捕20人

制作人：副督察长洛根 转呈人：督察长克劳福德 （批注：6/5/44 G-J）

1940年4月23日上午10时30分，上海船坞有限公司经理邦尼曼（Bonnyman）先生致电称，他掌握情报显示，罢工主要头目在法租界贝勒路33号春江（Chuen Kiang）三号旅馆78号房间设有办事处，并且他们威胁浦东国际船坞的第二号装配工，令其于1940年4月23日上午前往上述房间讨论国际船坞的局势，该处全体工人已复工。邦尼曼先生表示，他认为罢工者企图进一步恐吓浦东国际船坞的工人，迫使他们再次停工，从而协助他们在杨树浦船坞解决罢工问题。邦尼曼先生紧急请求警方突袭上述工会办事处，以避免对国际船坞工人进行进一步的恐吓。

在附属于乔佛瑞哨所（Post Joffre）的法国警方的协助下，副督察长洛根和特别支部警探281号（C.D.S. 281）走访了

（印：SPECIAL POLICE REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 8944/1 Station, Date 23rd April 40. 19）

Subject Shanghai Dockyards Ltd. - Strike.

Made by D. S. I. Logan. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

（批：No 6/2/44 A.I.）

At 2.30 p.m., 22-4-40, Mr. Bonnyman and
Mr. Beattie, Manager and Works Superintendent,
respectively of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., called
at the Special Branch in order to solicit the opinion
of the Police as to the advisability of adopting any
or all of the undermentioned measures, viz :-
(1) The Company to write a letter to the three chief
strike leaders namely, No.116 Yih Ching Hwa
( 葉錦華 ), No.206 Sze Wei Ming ( 施惠民 )
and Chang Sian Dee ( 張小弟 ) notifying them
that they are dismissed and therefore their
presence will not be tolerated anywhere in any of
the Company's yards.
(2) The Police, with the assistance of the French
Police, to search the rendezvous of the strike
leaders at Room 78 of the Tsung Kiang Lodging-
house, 63 Rue Palikao French Concession and
seize all books and documents belonging to the
Union which might be found there.
N.B. In this connection Mr. Bonnyman suggested that
it is not improbable that something like a bullet,
pistol or dagger might be found which would justify
legal action against the strike leaders.
It is known to the Police that one of the
strikers who is an informer of the Company is a

Chu Yu Ching is stated to have given a
cocktail party at the Astor House Hotel on
5-4-40, to which representatives of foreign
firms in Pootung were invited. At this party,
Chu Yu Ching promised the foreign representatives
that he would do all in his power to protect the
interests of foreigners in Pootung. The cocktail
party is believed to have been part of a campaign
to improve relations between the Authorities and
foreign firms in Pootung with a view to persuading
the latter to pay taxes. Mr. Bonnyman was
informed that the points raised would be
forwarded in report form.

Meanwhile the general strike continues.
It is known that on 22-4-40, some 80 workers turned
up for work at the International Dock, Pootung. This
dock is now operating with practically full complement
while the labour situation in the Tungkafoo dock is
also nearly normal this morning, April 23rd.

据称，Chu Yu Ching 于 1940 年 4 月 5 日在礼查饭店（Astor House Hotel）举办了一场鸡尾酒会，邀请了在浦东的外国公司代表参加。在此次酒会上，Chu Yu Ching 向外国代表承诺，他将竭尽全力保护外国人在浦东的利益。据信，这场鸡尾酒会是旨在改善当局与浦东外国公司之间关系的一场运动的一部分，目的是劝说后者缴纳税款。Bonnyman 先生获悉，所提出的问题将以报告形式转呈。

与此同时，总罢工仍在继续。据悉，1940 年 4 月 22 日，约有 80 名工人前往浦东国际码头（International Dock）上班。该码头目前几乎满员运作，而东卡夫（Tungkafoo）码头的劳工状况在 4 月 23 日上午也几近正常。

Made by D.S.I. Logan, Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

（左侧手写批注：D. S. I. 676 Yulee Rd.）

At 11.30 a.m., c.4.40, Mr. Bonnyman, Manager
of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., reported by telephone
that his company had hired two welders from
the Nanfang Company, 137 Rue Marco Polo but that
they had ceased to work for him after having
received a letter from Koh Siu Ngao (郭秀岩) and
Sze Yu Foo (施幼富), lawyers engaged by the
workmen's Union. asking them not to do anything
that would help to break the strike. D.S.I. Logan
and C.D.C. 107 (Special Branch) with the assistance
of the French Police visited 137 Rue Marco Polo
at 3 p.m., 8.4.40 and interviewed one Kan Cha Zien
(甘階笙), Manager of the Nanfang Co.. who stated
that the letter in question had been delivered by
messenger on 7.4.40 to above address. Mr. Kan
handed the letter over to D.S.I. Logan on condition
it will be returned to him should he ask for it.
According to Mr. Kan, six persons claiming to be
representatives of the strikers called at his home
on the night of 6.4.40 and asked him not to hire
any of his workmen to the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd.
as such action would help to break their strike.
They did not use any threats or intimidation but
appealed to him not to do anything that would
prejudice their strike. From the description
of two of the callers it would appear that they
were No. 116 Yih Chino Hwa (叶錦華) and No. 206
Sze Wei Ming (施惠民).

上午11时30分，约4时40分，上海船坞有限公司经理邦尼曼（Bonnyman）先生电话报告称，该公司从马可孛罗路137号南方公司雇佣了两名焊工，但这两人在收到工人联合会聘请的律师郭秀岩（Koh Siu Ngao）和施幼富（Sze Yu Foo）的来信后，已停止为其工作。信中要求他们不要做任何有助于破坏罢工的事情。副警司洛根与特别支部第107号华籍侦探长，在法国巡捕的协助下，于1940年4月8日下午3时走访了马可孛罗路137号，并面谈了南方公司经理甘階笙（Kan Cha Zien）先生。甘先生称，上述信件已于1940年4月7日由信差送至上述地址。甘先生将该信交给副警司洛根，条件是若他日后索要，须将信归还。据甘先生称，1940年4月6日晚，六名自称是罢工者代表的人来到他家，要求他不要将其任何工人雇佣给上海船坞有限公司，因为此举将有助于破坏他们的罢工。他们未使用任何威胁或恐吓手段，而是恳请他不要做任何有损其罢工的事。根据对其中两名来访者的描述，他们似乎是叶錦華（Yih Chino Hwa，编号116）和施惠民（Sze Wei Ming，编号206）。

Translation of a letter received by the Nan Fang
Electric Welding Company, 37 Rue Marco Polo, from
lawyers KOH SIU NGAO and SZE YU FOO, at 9 a.m.,7/4/40
......

To Manager,
Nan Fang Electric Welding Co.,
37 Rue Marco Polo.

Sir,

We beg to inform you of the following statement
by our clients, the representatives of the Workers'
Union of the Shanghai Dockyards :

"All legal cases relative to this Union have been
referred to you for disposal. This Union is organized
on a sound basis, whereby some 1,000 labour friends
are safeguarded in connection with their employment.
Reports have been received from workers that prior
to the settlement of the dispute between the Union
and the management, the Nan Fang Electric Welding
Company ( 南方電焊公司 ) is engaging employees
on behalf of the management. Such steps affect this
Union to a considerable extent. Please send a
written request to the Nan Fang Electric Welding
Company to cease forthwith such practice which is
to the detriment of the Union, otherwise the Nan
Fang Company will be held responsible for the
extension of the dispute. Please convey the above
to the Nan Fang Electric Welding Company."

We therefore inform you of the above statement
in accordance with the request of our clients. You are
requested to send members to our offices within two days
to have a talk in order to avoid any misunderstanding.

(Chopped): KOH SIU NGAO, lawyer
( 郭少敖 )
SZE YU FOO "
( 施幼孚 )

南方电焊公司（位于马可波罗路37号）于1940年4月7日上午9时收到律师郭少敖（KOH SIU NGAO）和施幼孚（SZE YU FOO）来信的译文
 ____ 

致经理，
南方电焊公司，
马可波罗路37号。

先生：

兹奉我方委托人，即上海船坞工人联合会代表之嘱，告知如下声明：

“所有与本联合会有关的法律案件均已移交贵方处理。本联合会组织健全，旨在保障约一千名劳工友人在就业方面的权益。据工人报告，在联合会与管理层之间的纠纷解决之前，南方电焊公司（ 南方電焊公司 ）正代表管理层招募员工。此类举措对本联合会影响甚大。请向南方电焊公司发出书面要求，立即停止这种损害联合会利益的行为，否则南方公司将须对纠纷的扩大承担责任。请将上述内容转达给南方电焊公司。”

At 11 a.m. April 4, two delegates of the
Shanghai Dockyards' workers named Chen Ping Kong
(陳炳康) and Sz Wei Ming (施惠民) called
at Special Branch and delivered a letter stating
that the 11 delegates have resigned from their
positions as workers' representatives. (full
translation attached)

At 12 noon April 4, ten of the eleven
delegates visited the Dockyards and notified the
management in a like manner. While they were on
the premises, some 200 workers gathered on a piece
of vacant ground on Yangtszepoo Road opposite the
Dockyards with, it is believed, a view to safeguarding
the delegates from being arrested by the Municipal
Police. Some of these workers are reported to
have stated that they intended to assault Mr. Beattie,
the foreign supervisor. They, however, left quietly
at 1 p.m.

On the afternoon of April 4, the management
posted a notice to the effect that approved workmen
might return to work under the terms of the old
agreement plus an increase of 10% in wages. (full
text mentioned in report dated April 4)

April 5, to take place on the same piece of vacant
ground. About 500 workers attended, but owing to

NOTICE TO THE REGULAR WORKMEN
OF
SHANGHAI DOCKYARDS LTD.

As the Company believe the workmen are not being told
all the facts by the so-called Union Committee regarding the
matters discussed at the various meetings in this Office,
the Company now make the following statement:-

The Company have never accepted the Committee of eleven
delegates (consisting largely of unskilled, semi-skilled, and
temporary workmen) as true representatives of the workmen, but
nevertheless have continued to listen to them in order to
negotiate, if possible, any of the first set of demands and
conditions put forward. Most of these first conditions were
rejected by the Company as being unreasonable and impossible
for any business concern to agree to, the Company
told the Committee so
verbally on Saturday, 23rd March, and confirmed it in writing
to them on 26th March, asking them to modify the demands
sufficiently to enable the Company to compromise if possible.

On March 27th, the Committee then requested a meeting
with the Company and this was arranged for Friday, 29th March,
when the Union Committee told the Management their modified
and final demands. The Management asked the Committee for
this in writing so that there should be no misunderstanding.
The Committee at first refused but finally agreed, and eventually
the Company received the letter confirming the so-called
modified demands. The Company's official and final terms
were handed to the Union on 2nd April.

It is regretted very much by the Company that they cannot
now make any further negotiation with the Committee as their
conditions are unreasonable and we cannot comply with them,
especially as we know that the Committee told the workmen that
the Company had practically agreed to most of the demands and
conditions, whereas this is entirely untrue as no reply was

鉴于本公司认为，所谓工会委员会并未就本办公室各次会议所讨论的事项向工人们告知全部事实，本公司现发表如下声明：

本公司从未承认由十一名代表组成的委员会（其成员主要为非熟练工、半熟练工及临时工）为工人的真正代表，但为了就可能提出的第一批要求与条件进行谈判，本公司仍继续听取他们的意见。这些首批条件中的大多数被本公司视为不合理，且任何商业机构均无法同意，本公司已于3月23日（星期六）口头告知委员会此点，并于3月26日以书面形式予以确认，要求他们对要求作出充分修改，以便本公司在可能的情况下达成妥协。

3月27日，委员会随后请求与本公司举行会议，该会议安排在3月29日（星期五）举行。届时，工会委员会向管理层提出了其修改后的最终要求。管理层要求委员会将此以书面形式提交，以免产生误解。委员会起初拒绝，但最终同意，随后本公司收到了确认所谓修改后要求的信函。本公司的正式最终条款已于4月2日移交给工会。

本公司深感遗憾，目前无法再与委员会进行任何进一步谈判，因其条件不合理，我方无法遵从；尤其因为我们获悉，委员会曾告诉工人，本公司实际上已同意大部分要求和条件，而此说法完全不实，因为并未回复

先生们：

我方已收到贵方对3月18日协议草案的最终修订案，该修订案于上月30日（星期六）下午12时45分交予我方比蒂（Beattie）先生。兹回复如下：

我方毫无理由修改以往协议中既有的条款，该条款多年来已成惯例。若有工人不认同此条款，可另谋他就。我方无法同意此项修改。

若旧协议第(1)款保持不变，且能提供令人满意的保证，确保公司之业务不因工会之存在而受到掣肘，我方愿每月向工会捐助100.00美元，用于维持办事处之开支。

page_data.en:
TRANSLATION

The following is the final amendment to the draft
agreement submitted by workers on the afternoon of
March 18. Please give a definite reply before April 3,
1940.

Right of the Union

1. The Company must recognize the Union's right to
represent the workmen of the various departments,
such as Fitters, Turners, Carpenters, Electric Welders,
Foundry Workers, Electricians, Coppersmiths, and all
coolies of the dockyards. In accordance with the
provisions of the Chinese Factory Law, the term
"workmen" denotes those who are either directly
engaged or assisting in the productive services.
Though the standard of education of the workers in
the various departments is different, they are equal
in respect of personality and human rights. Therefore,
no difference shall be made relating to the rights
and obligations of the workmen because of the
difference in the standard of education.

2. The object of this Union is to devise means to
promote the welfare for the workmen, and to promote
good relations between labour and capital. The
Company should grant the Union a monthly allowance
of $100.00 and provide the latter with an office.
Two members of the Standing Committee will work
regularly in the Union offices to deal with labour
disputes on behalf of the workmen, and they should
be paid due wages by the company.

Bonus

3. The Company agrees to appropriate 65% of its profits
for distribution among the workmen as bonuses. The
minimum bonus to be received by workmen shall be equal
to a sum not less than half a month's pay.

Termination of Service
page_data.zh:
译文

以下为工人于3月18日下午提交的协议草案之最终修订案。请于1940年4月3日前给予明确答复。

工会权利

1. 公司必须承认工会有权代表各部门工人，如装配工、车工、木工、电焊工、铸造工、电工、铜匠以及船坞的所有苦力。根据《中国工厂法》的规定，“工人”一词系指直接从事或协助生产服务的人员。尽管各部门工人的教育程度不同，但他们在人格和人权方面是平等的。因此，不得因教育程度的差异而在工人的权利和义务方面有所区别。

2. 本工会的宗旨在于制定措施以促进工人福利，并促进劳资之间的良好关系。公司应每月向工会提供100.00美元的津贴，并为工会提供办公场所。常务委员会的两名成员将在工会办公室定期工作，代表工人处理劳资纠纷，其工资应由公司照常支付。

奖金

3. 公司同意将其利润的65%拨出，作为奖金分发给工人。工人获得的最低奖金数额应不少于半个月工资。

解雇

page_data.en:
-2-

Termination of Service

4. The Company agrees not to dismiss any workmen owing
to business depression. However, the Company has
the right to terminate the service of workmen for
any of the following offences:-
(A) Insubordination.
(B) Theft.
(C) Continued or malicious breach of the Company's
rules more than three times.
(Reason) : The prosperity or depression of trade of a
company or a business shop is determined by its
profits gained or losses sustained. For instance,
a company, though it appears to be very prosperous,
may sustain losses. Therefore, its business can be
considered to be sound. On the contrary, a company,
though it appears to be in a state of business
slackness, may gain huge profits. Consequently, we
cannot say that such company is in a state of
business depression. Our company differs from other
concerns. There may be plenty of work both day and
night, when ships are required to undergo repair,
and services will not be necessary when no one applies
to our company for ship repairing. As a matter of
fact, our company is not in a state of business
depression but receives good profits every year. The
4th condition is drawn up and based upon this reason.

Work by Turn

When necessary in time of business depression, the
Company may make arrangements for the workmen to have
work by turn. The company agrees to guarantee
employment to workmen for not less than 18 days in
every 28 days, and to pay full rice allowance (for
non-working days ??) . The work-by-turn system
shall only be applied when there is work for only half
of the total **〔此处转录不清〕** complement of workmen.
page_data.zh:
-2-

终止雇佣

4. 公司同意不因商业萧条而解雇任何工人。然而，公司有权因下列任何过失终止工人的雇佣：
(A) 不服从管理。
(B) 盗窃。
(C) 连续或恶意违反公司规定三次以上。
（理由）：一家公司或商号的贸易繁荣或萧条，取决于其获得的利润或遭受的损失。例如，一家公司虽然表面上看起来非常繁荣，但可能会遭受损失。因此，其业务不能被视为健全。相反，一家公司虽然表面上处于业务清淡状态，但可能会获得巨额利润。因此，我们不能说该公司处于商业萧条状态。本公司与其他企业不同。当船舶需要修理时，日夜都可能有大量工作；而当无人向本公司申请修船时，则不需要服务。事实上，本公司并未处于商业萧条状态，而是每年均获得良好的利润。第4条条款即基于此理由制定。

轮班工作

在商业萧条时期如有必要，公司可安排工人轮流工作。公司同意保证每28天内为工人提供不少于18天的就业，并支付全额米贴（用于非工作日？？）。轮班工作制仅适用于工作量仅够全部**〔此处转录不清〕**编制工人的一半时。

page_data.en:
-3-

Leave

6. Workmen shall have ten holidays with full pay in
every year. Workmen who operate on holidays shall
be given extra-day's pay; those working for night
shift on holidays shall be granted normal night-
shift wages. The holidays are as follows:-
January 1 and 2. Two days.
March 12.
Easter Holiday.
May 1.
October 10.
November 12.
December 25.
1st and 2nd days of the 1st month, Lunar New Year -
two days.

Accidents and compensation

7 In the case of any workman who is injured in the
performance of duty, the Company agrees to grant him
medical expenses, and to pay him full wages and rice
allowance for a period not exceeding three months
during which he is under medical treatment. If the
workman is still incapable or permanently disabled
or dies on the expiry of three months' period, the
Company agrees to pay to his next of kin a
compassionate and retiring gratuity of $500.00.
The foregoing benefits will be granted provided
the injured workman agrees to receive treatment
immediately after an accident, at any of the
following hospitals:-
(A) St. Luke's Hospital.
(B) Lester Hospital, Shantung Road.
(C) Paulun Hospital.
(D) American Red Cross Hospital.
(E) Tientsin Road Red Cross Hospital.
(F) Blue Cross Hospital.

8. In the event of the natural death of any workman from
sickness or if he is incapacitated from active

休假

6. 工人每年享有十天带薪假期。在假日工作的工人应获得额外一天的工资；在假日值夜班的工人应获得正常的夜班工资。假期如下：-
1月1日和2日。两天。
3月12日。
复活节假期。
5月1日。
10月10日。
11月12日。
12月25日。
农历正月初一和初二 - 两天。

事故与赔偿

7. 如有任何工人在执行职务时受伤，公司同意向其提供医疗费用，并在其接受治疗期间（不超过三个月）支付全额工资及米贴。如果该工人在三个月期满时仍无法工作、永久残疾或死亡，公司同意向其最近亲属支付慰问及退休酬金500.00美元。上述福利的发放，以受伤工人同意在事故发生后立即前往下列任何一家医院接受治疗为前提：-
(A) 圣路加医院 (St. Luke's Hospital)。
(B) 山东路莱斯特医院 (Lester Hospital, Shantung Road)。

8. 如有任何工人因病自然死亡，或因病丧失活动能力

concerning death or inpecitation of a workman

doctor.

9. In the case of a workman who is incapacitated through
old age, the Company agrees to pay him retirement
allowance in accordance with the following scale:-

9. 若工人因年老而丧失工作能力，公司同意按下列标准向其支付退休金：-

工龄不满10年者：无。

工龄超过10年但不满15年者：150元。

工龄超过25年但不满30年者：400元。

工龄超过30年者：500元。

学徒

10. 公司同意按下列标准向学徒支付报酬：-

第一年每日40分。
第二年每日50分。
第三年每日60分。
第四年每日70分。
第五年每日80分。

公司在学徒服务满五年后可将其解雇，但无论予以留用还是解雇，均须向其颁发证书。该证书应注明其已忠实且良好地履行了学徒职责，并已成为本行业的熟练技工（master journeyman）。此证书仅授予那些已彻底掌握其技艺，且在公司服务期间总体品行和行为表现令人满意的学徒。若

apprentices be retained in the service of the
Company, after their apprenticeship is completed,
the Company agrees to increase their pay according
to their efficiency.

Stoppage or work or strike

11. The Company should be informed of any dissatisfaction
on the part of workmen, and the workmen shall not
create a stoppage of work without first giving the
company 48 hours' notice of any reason. In the
event of a strike being declared without
authorization, the workmen involved in the strike
will automatically forfeit all the privileges due
to them under this Agreement. Any workmen who are
found wilfully or maliciously damaging the Company's
property or intimidating other workmen from operating
shall be dismissed from the Company's service, and
forfeit all benefits due them.

In the event of a strike being declared by a number
of workmen, the Company will not be responsible for
the payment of wages to those for whom work is not
available by reason of the strike. The workmen,
however, will not be subject to such restriction if
the company breaks this Agreement.

Rice Allowance

12. The Company agrees to continue the issue of rice
allowance to all workmen on the basis of the prices
of "Kan Mee" of Changshu and Wusieh origin as
published in the local "Sin Wan Pao" every Monday.
(If Changshu and Wusieh rice is unavailable, the
price of 1st quality Saigon rice shall be taken as
the standard.)

The scale of rice allowance is given below:-

学徒在学徒期结束后若继续受雇于本公司，本公司同意根据其工作效率提高其薪资。

停工或罢工

11. 工人如有任何不满，应告知本公司；工人在未提前48小时通知公司任何理由的情况下，不得制造停工。如发生未经授权的罢工，参与罢工的工人将自动丧失本协议项下赋予他们的所有特权。凡发现故意或恶意损坏公司财产或恐吓其他工人使其无法工作的工人，将被解除雇佣关系，并丧失其应得的所有福利。

如因部分工人宣布罢工，导致其他工人无工可做，本公司不负责支付这些工人的工资。然而，如果本公司违反本协议，则工人不受此限制。

米贴

12. 本公司同意继续向所有工人发放米贴，计算基准为当地《新闻报》每周一刊登的常熟和无锡产“粳米”价格。（如无常熟和无锡米供应，则以一等西贡米的价格为标准。）

Pay for night work and work on Sundays

13. The Company agrees to pay one and half hours' wages
    for one hour's night work and so on, and to issue
    a half day's wages to workmen who observe Sunday
    as holiday.   The Company will issue one and half
    days' wages for workmen working on Sunday.

1. Full pay and rice allowance for the period of strike.
2. Increase in wages by 50 cents per day per workman.
3. $1.00 food allowance for any workman when he is
    required to work at some other place and unable
    to return to the Company for his meals but the
    rice allowance for that day shall be abolished.
4. 20 cents of "soap" allowance per day per workman
    employed in filthy work.

At 3 p.m., March 29, 1940, the eleven
representatives of the workmen called on the
management of the Company. Mr. Bonnyman, Manager,
addressed the delegates and drew their attention
to the various instances of good treatment of
the workers by the Company, e.g. provision of
steam launches to transport the workers during
the first months of the local hostilities, the
granting of a loan to the workers to tide them
over the first few weeks of the local hostilities,
etc., in order to refute certain allegations by
the workers contained in a letter addressed to
the Board of Directors of the Company. The reply
of the Company to the strikers' demands was then
discussed and the workmen verbally agreed to certain
minor modifications in their demands. They also
agreed to submit these modifications in writing to
the Company on March 30, 1940. The Company's
reply to same will be handed to the delegates on
April 3, 1940. At 11 a.m., March 30, 1940, Mr.
Beattie, Works Manager, reported that he had
received information from a reliable source to the
effect that shortly after 5 p.m., March 29, 1940,
the delegates addressed about 100 workers on the
result of their meeting with the management and
in doing so misrepresented the reply of the
management as being more favourable to the workers

At 10 a.m., March 23th, 1940, the management
of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., received in the
Company's office, the eleven representatives of the
workers and in general terms discussed the demands
presented by the workers to the Company through the
eleven representatives on March 18th, 1940 (Special
Branch Report 20-3-40). The management informed
the representatives that the Company's written reply
to the demands of the workers would be handed to the
workers' representatives on March 26th, 1940. On
March 22, 1940, Mr. Amour, Assistant Manager of the
Company, requested the Special Branch to communicate
to the workers' representatives the desire of the
management that payment of two days' wages and rice
allowance due on March 23, 1940, should be postponed.
This was done and the representatives gave an assurance
that the desire of the management would be complied
with. However, some 100 workers turned up at 9.30
a.m., March 23, 1940 with the intention to draw their
wages. The management anticipating that this might
happen made preparations to make payment but when one of
the workmen stepped forward to collect his wages, a
coolie worker, Mang Ching Yue (滿金玉), 42,
Tsingkiang, 110 Zang An Li, Yangtsepoo Road, shouted
instructions to him not to draw his wages and was
immediately arrested by F. S. Phinn. Enquiries
revealed that the coolie had been requested by the

Made by. D. S. I. Logan. Forwarded by. Supt. J. Mason.

Between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m., March 16,
approximately 300 workers of the Shanghai Dockyards,
640 Y'poo Road held a meeting on a piece of ground at
the corner of Y'poo and Jansen Roads. Sz Wei Ming
(施惠明), Yih Ching Hwa (葉錦華) alias Yih Mao Deu
(葉七頭) and Zung Ah Kong (陳阿庚), three
representatives of workers of the Shanghai Dockyards,
spoke to the workers and announced the new demands which
are to be submitted to the management. It was decided
that a letter be addressed by Yih Ching Hwa to the
workers of the Shanghai Dockyards at Pootung asking
them to appoint representatives to participate in
discussion for a general strike. Should the letter be
ignored, workers will be despatched to Pootung to
solicit cooperation.

The representatives of the strikers are
known to have established a rendezvous at Room 67, San
Fang Lodging House, Rue Paliko.

Subject. Shanghai Dockyards - workers present demands.

Made by D.S.I. Logan. Forwarded by Supt. J. Mason.

At 2.30 p.m. March 18, eleven workers
claiming to represent all the workers of the Shanghai
Dockyards, with the exception of foremen, called on
the management at 640 Yangtszepoo Road. Apart from
presenting signatures of some 950 workers who appointed
them to be their representatives, they submitted the
draft of a new labour agreement for consideration.
They were received by the manager, who informed them
that the documents would be translated and passed to
the Board of Directors, and should a reply come, the
delegates would be informed through the Police. No
time limit was given them.

Attached is a translation of the draft of
labour agreement submitted.

Translation of a draft agreement submitted
to the management by workers of the
Shanghai Dockyards on March 18, 1940.

Agreement made this ............ day of ............,
1940, between the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., hereinafter referred to
as the "Company", and the union of workmen of the Shanghai
Dockyards Ltd., hereinafter referred to as the "Union ", whereby
it is mutually agreed as follows :-

Right of the Union

1. The Company recognizes the Union's right to represent the
whole body of workmen with badges and recognizes all
workmen, new and old, as permanent employees.

2. The Company agrees to grant the Union a monthly allowance of
$150.00 for its up-keep and to pay the wages of two members
of the Standing Committee of the Union who will be appointed
by the Union to deal with disputes between labour and
capital and to undertake regular work in the Union instead
of performing work in the dockyards.

Bonus

3. The Company agrees to pay each workman a bonus equal to one
month's pay at the end of every year.

Termination of Service

4. The Company agrees not to dismiss any workman owing to
business depression. However, the Company may terminate the
service of workmen for any of the following offences :-
(A) Insubordination.
(B) Theft or dishonesty.
(C) Continued or malicious breach of the Company's
general rules.
page_data.zh:
上海船坞工人于1940年3月18日提交给管理层的协议草案译文。

本协议由上海船坞有限公司（以下简称“公司”）与上海船坞有限公司工人工会（以下简称“工会”）于1940年____月____日订立，双方达成如下共识：

工会的权利

1. 公司承认工会有权代表全体佩戴徽章的工人，并承认所有新老工人为正式雇员。

2. 公司同意每月向工会提供150.00元的津贴，用于其日常开支，并支付工会常务委员会两名成员的工资；这两名成员将由工会指派，负责处理劳资纠纷，并在工会从事常规工作，以此代替在船坞内的作业。

奖金

3. 公司同意在每年年底向每位工人发放相当于一个月工资的奖金。

解雇

4. 公司同意不因业务萧条而解雇任何工人。然而，若工人犯有以下任何过错，公司可终止其雇佣关系：
(A) 不服从管理。
(B) 盗窃或不诚实行为。
(C) 持续或恶意违反公司的一般规章。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Work by turn
When necessary i. time of business depression the
Company may make arrangements for the workmen to have work by
turn. The Company agrees to guarantee employment to workmen
for a minimum of 18 days in every 28 days, and to pay half
wages and full rice allowance for non-working days.
The work-by-turn system shall only be applied when
there is work for only half the number of workmen.

Leave
Workmen shall have ten holidays with full pay in
every year. If they work on these days, irrespective of
whether it is day or night work, they shall be given extra-pay
equal to 200% of their original wages.
The holidays are listed hereunder :-
January 1 and 2.
March 12.
Easter Holiday.
May 1.
October 10.
November 12.
December 25.
Lunar new year days, 1st and 2nd.

Accidents and compensation
7. The Company agrees to grant, in the case of any workman
who is injured in the performance of his duty, medical expenses,
and to pay him full wages and rice allowance for a period not
exceeding three months. At the end of three months, if the man
is still incapable or permanently disabled or dies, the Company
agrees to pay to his next of kin a compassionate and Retiring
grant of $500.00.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

轮班工作
如有必要，即在业务萧条时期，公司可安排工人轮流工作。公司同意保证每28天内至少为工人提供18天的工作，并在非工作日支付半薪及全额米贴。
轮班工作制仅适用于工作量仅够半数工人从事的情况。

休假
工人每年享有十天带薪假日。若在这些日子工作，无论是日班还是夜班，均应获得相当于原工资200%的额外薪酬。
假日列表如下：
1月1日和2日。
3月12日。
复活节假期。
5月1日。
10月10日。
11月12日。
12月25日。
农历新年初一和初二。

工伤与赔偿
7. 公司同意，对于任何在履行职责过程中受伤的工人，报销其医疗费用，并在不超过三个月的期限内向其支付全额工资及米贴。三个月期满后，若该工人仍无法工作、永久残疾或死亡，公司同意向其最近亲属支付一笔金额为500.00元的抚恤金及退休金。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

The foregoing benefits will be granted only if the
injured workman agrees to receive treatment immediately after
the accident, at any one of the following hospitals :-
(1) St. Luke's Hospital.
(2) Lester Chinese Hospital.
(3) Paulun Hospital.
(4) American Red Cross Hospital.
(5) Red Cross Hospital, Tientsin Road.
(6) Blue Cross Hospital.

8. In the event of the natural death of any workman
from sickness or if he is incapacitated from active service
through sickness and has to retire, the Company agrees to pay
to such workman or his next of kin a compassionate grant of
$400.00. Satisfactory proof of death or incapacitation must
be submitted from a recognized and qualified doctor.

9. In the case of a workman who is incapacitated
through old age, the Company agrees to pay him retirement
allowance in accordance with the following scale :-
Workmen of under 10 years' service : nil.
Workmen of above 10 years' service and under 15 years'
service : $150.
Workmen of above 15 Years' service and under 20 years'
service : $200.
Workmen of above 15 Years' Service and under 25 years'
service : $300.

Apprentices

10. The Company agrees to pay apprentices according
to the following scale :-
56 cents per day for the 1st year.
66 " " " " " 2nd "
78 " " " " " 3rd "
$1.00 " " " " " 4th "
$1.30 " " " " " 5th "
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

上述福利仅在受伤工人同意于事故发生后立即前往下列任一医院接受治疗的情况下方可授予：
(1) 圣路加医院 (St. Luke's Hospital)。
(2) 雷士德华人医院 (Lester Chinese Hospital)。
(3) 宝隆医院 (Paulun Hospital)。
(4) 美国红十字会医院 (American Red Cross Hospital)。
(5) 天津路红十字会医院 (Red Cross Hospital, Tientsin Road)。
(6) 蓝十字医院 (Blue Cross Hospital)。

8. 如有任何工人因病自然死亡，或因病丧失工作能力而必须退休，公司同意向该工人或其最近亲属支付抚恤金 400.00 元。必须提交由公认且具备资格的医生出具的死亡或丧失工作能力的有效证明。

9. 对于因年老而丧失工作能力的工人，公司同意按以下标准向其支付退休金：
工龄不满 10 年的工人：无。
工龄超过 10 年但不满 15 年的工人：150 元。
工龄超过 15 年但不满 20 年的工人：200 元。
工龄超过 15 年但不满 25 年的工人：300 元。

学徒

10. 公司同意按以下标准向学徒支付工资：
第 1 年：每日 56 分。
第 2 年：每日 66 分。
第 3 年：每日 78 分。
第 4 年：每日 1.00 元。
第 5 年：每日 1.30 元。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

11. The Company may discharge any apprentice after
five years' service, but has to give him a certificate
irrespective of whether he is retained or discharged. The
certificate should mention that he has served his apprenticeship
faithfully and well and has become a skilled master journeyman
of the trade. It will only be granted to such apprentices
after they have thoroughly learnt their trades and their
general conduct and behaviour while in the service of the
Company, has been satisfactory. Should apprentices be retained
in the service of the Company, after their apprenticeship is
completed, the Company agrees to increase their pay according
to their efficiency.

Stoppage of work or strike

12. The Company should be informed 48 hours beforehand
if the workmen intend to declare a strike owing to dissatisfac-
tion. However, this notification is not required if the
strike is declared owing to a breach of the agreement on the
part of the Company.

Rice Allowance

13. The Company agrees to continue the issue of rice
allowance to all workmen on the basis of the prices of "Kan Mee"
of Changchow and Wusieh origin as published in the local press
on every Monday. If Wusieh and Changchow rice is unavailable,
the price of 1st quality Saigon rice shall be taken as the
standard. The Company agrees to pay full rice allowance to
workmen who have been out of work for less than two weeks.

Scale of rice allowance

| Price of rice | Allowance |
| :--- | :--- |
| From $20.10 to $30 per "zar" | $2 per week (6 working days) per capita. |
| From $30.10 to $40 per "zar" | $3 per week per capita. |
| From $40.10 to $50 per "zar" | $4 " " " " |
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

11. 公司可在学徒服务满五年后将其解雇，但无论予以留用还是解雇，均须向其颁发证书。该证书应注明其已忠实且良好地履行了学徒义务，并已成为本行业技术熟练的出师工匠。只有在学徒彻底掌握其技艺，且在公司服务期间的一般品行与表现令人满意的情况下，方可向其颁发此证书。若学徒在学徒期满后继续受雇于公司，公司同意根据其工作效率提高其薪资。

停工或罢工

12. 若工人因不满而意图宣布罢工，应提前48小时通知公司。然而，若罢工是因公司违反协议所致，则无需发出此通知。

米贴

13. 公司同意继续向所有工人发放米贴，计算基础为每周一当地报刊刊登的常州和无锡产“粳米”价格。若无无锡和常州大米供应，则以一等西贡米的价格作为标准。公司同意向失业不足两周的工人全额支付米贴。

米贴标准

| 米价 | 津贴 |
| :--- | :--- |
| 每“担”20.10元至30元 | 每人每周（6个工作日）2元。 |
| 每“担”30.10元至40元 | 每人每周3元。 |
| 每“担”40.10元至50元 | 每人每周4元。 |

page_data.en:
- 5 -

Price of rice                                Allowance
From $50.10 to $60.00 per "zar"              $6.00 per week per capita.

The Company also agrees to continue the issue of rice
allowance to apprentices, equivalent to 60% of the above scale.

Pay for night work and work on Sundays

14.        The Company agrees to pay two hours' wages for one
hour's night work and so on, and to issue full pay to workmen
who observe Sunday as holiday.    The Company will issue double
pay for work on Sundays.

------------------

Demands :-

1.    Full pay and rice allowance for the period of strike.
2.    Dismissal of the Russian watchman who tore up a notice
      on March 14.
3.    Launch service for workers residing this side of the
      Whangpoo.
4.    Increase in wages by $1.00 per day per workman.
5.    $1.00 food allowance for any workman when he is required
      to work at some other place and unable to return to the
      Company for his meals.
6.    20 cents of "soap" allowance per day per workman employed
      in filthy work.
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

米价                                    津贴
每“担”从 $50.10 至 $60.00              每人每周 $6.00。

公司亦同意继续向学徒发放米贴，数额相当于上述标准的 60%。

夜班及星期日工作工资

14.        公司同意按一小时夜班支付两小时工资，依此类推，并向将星期日视为休假日的工人发放全额工资。公司将对星期日工作发放双倍工资。

---

要求：-

1.    罢工期间发放全额工资及米贴。
2.    开除于 3 月 14 日撕毁通告的俄国看守人。
3.    为居住在黄浦江此岸的工人提供轮渡服务。
4.    每名工人每日增加工资 $1.00。
5.    任何工人若被要求在其他地点工作且无法回公司用餐，发给 $1.00 膳食津贴。
6.    从事肮脏工作的每名工人每日发给 20 分“肥皂”津贴。

Subject Shanghai Dockyards - workers declare a "tai-kung" strike.
（手写批注：No. 5/3/44）

Made by D. I. Lorn. Forwarded by Supt. J. Luson. （手写签名：A. I.）

Some 1,000 workers of the Shanghai Dockyards,
640 Yangtszepoo Road, declared a "tai-kung" strike at
11 a.m. March 16.

On March 12, 1940, the unskilled workers
complained that the management failed to observe the
labour agreement signed on December 6, 1939, in
respect of the issue of rice allowance for the period
of suspension of work. The agreement stipulates
that rice allowance be granted to tradesman during
the period of suspension of work but does not make
provision for the issue of rice to unskilled workers
during suspension. At 11 a.m. March 14, the
leaders of the unskilled workers attempted to post
a notice in the dockyard with a view to calling for
a general meeting of workers to discuss the complaint,
but the removal of the notice by a Russian watchman
resulted in the latter being assaulted by the coolies
and it would appear that the fracas between the other
Russian watchmen and the coolies which followed the
assault, precipitated the strike.

At 3 p.m. March 16, Mr. P. Y. Koo of the
Industrial Section, S.M.C., who arranged the signing
of the labour agreement on December 6, 1939, attended
and endeavoured to persuade the workers to assist in

1940年3月12日，非技术工种工人抱怨资方未能遵守
1939年12月6日签署的劳工协议中关于停工期间发放米贴的规定。该协议规定，

非技术工种工人的领袖试图在船坞内张贴告示，
旨在召集工人大会以讨论该投诉，

随后其他俄国巡捕与苦力之间发生的冲突似乎加剧了事态，
从而引发了此次罢工。

3月16日下午3时，工务处（S.M.C. Industrial Section）的顾先生（Mr. P. Y. Koo），即安排签署

At 2.30 p.m., March 15, the eleven delegates
had an interview with the responsible members of the
management. D.S.I. Logan and D.S.I. Kao also attended.
The management explained that the workers had broken
the agreement by going on a "tai-kung" strike without
giving 48 hours notice and that if the workers had
any complaints to present, same should have been put
forward through the delegates who signed the previous
contract. Thereupon the workers stated that the
workers no longer trusted the original delegates and
declared that the eleven people mentioned were appointed
as the new delegates. The management refused to
negotiate with the new delegates until the resignation
of the old delegates is received and the names of the
new delegates are constitutionally put forward. The
workers thereupon stated that the matter would be
properly attended to and that they would return at
2.30 p.m. March 18. It is also expected that the
workers will submit their demands in writing.

    At 1 p.m. December 12th., 1939, the Chinese employees
of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 540, Yangtszepoo Road, ceased
work and gathered in the back compound, and signified their
intention not to resume until the management reached an
agreement on the question of the "Rice Allowance."

    At 2.30 p.m. December 12th., 1939, a meeting was held
between the representatives of the workers and the management,
at which Mr. P. Y. Ko, S.M.C/Industrial Section, and C.D.S.
235, attached to Yulin Road Station, were present.

    The representatives of the workers submitted demands
very similar to those outlined in the report forwarded yester-
day, and after lengthy negotiation, both parties agreed to the
following "Rice Allowance":-

    (1) When the price of rice ranges from $21.00 to $25.00
        per picul, an allowance of $1.25 per week will be paid.
    (2) $26.00 to $30.00, an allowance of $1.50 per week.
    (3) $31.00 to $40.00, an allowance of $2.00 per week.
    (4) $41.00 to $45.00, an allowance of $3.00 per week.
    (5) $46.00 to $50.00, an allowance of $4.00 per week.
Apprentices will be paid 60% of the above allowances.
The new "Rice Allowance" will commence from December 6th.,
1939.

    The night workers resumed as usual, and further trouble
is not expected.

Confidential.
16th REPORT
Yulin Road Station, 8941 A
Date December 11th 39.

Subject Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640 , Yangtsepoo Road.

Made by D.S.I. Ross. Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,
At 11.30 p.m. December 10th 1939, Mr. J. C. Armour,
manager, the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtsepoo Road,
telephoned the undersigned to the effect that he had certain
information which led him to believe that the workers intended
to present further demands to the company, on December 11th
1939.
It appears that the company had arranged that, on December
8th 1939, the workers should sign the agreement, which was
compiled at meetings held between representatives of the company
and the workers following the termination of the Strike on
November 26th 1939. However, on the mentioned date the repre-
sentatives of the workers refused to sign, on the grounds that
discontent existed regarding the present "Rice Allowance",
which was considered to be insufficient.
Mr. P. Y. Koo, S.M.C./Industrial Section, was present at
this meeting, but even this gentleman was unable to prevail
upon the representatives to sign.
According to Mr. Armour, during the week-end the workers
have held a meeting, at which they decided to present a demand
to the management for a much increased allowance, and setting
a time limit of 48 hours for a decision.
Detectives have been detailed to endeavour to obtain
information on the subject.
In the event of possible trouble at the Dockyards, the usual
Police precautions will be adopted.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
[签名]
D.S.I.

1939 年 12 月 10 日晚 11 时 30 分，杨树浦路 640 号上海船坞有限公司经理 J. C. Armour 先生致电卑职，称其掌握某些情报，使其相信工人拟于 1939 年 12 月 11 日向公司提出进一步要求。
据悉，公司曾安排工人于 1939 年 12 月 8 日签署协议，该协议系在 1939 年 11 月 26 日罢工结束后，由公司代表与工人代表举行的会议上拟定。然而，在上述日期，工人代表以目前“米贴”不足、引发不满为由，拒绝签署。
工部局工业科顾 P. Y. 先生出席了此次会议，但即便有这位先生在场，也未能说服代表们签字。
据 Armour 先生称，工人在周末举行了一次会议，决定向管理层提出大幅增加津贴的要求，并设定 48 小时为决策期限。
已指派侦探设法获取有关此事的情报。
若船坞发生可能的骚乱，将采取常规的警察预防措施。

AGREEMENT made this Thirtieth day of November One
Thousand Nine Hundred and Thirty Nine, between the Shanghai
Dockyards Ltd., hereinafter referred to as the "Company", and
the Workmen as defined in Para.1 employed by the Company,
thereinafter referred to as the "Workmen", whereby it is
mutually agreed as follows:-

WORKMEN
COVERED
BY AGREE-
MENT
(1) The Company recognises the Workmen's right to
represent the Fitters, Turners, Patternmakers, Coppersmiths,
Electricians, Welders, and Permanent Workshop Coolies employed
in the Company's various works.
No workman shall be entitled to the benefits arising out of
this Agreement until he shall have been in the continuous
employment of the Company for not less than 12 months.

BONUS
(2) The Company is prepared to pay to the Workmen a
bonus at the end of the year, provided the Company is able
to pay a dividend to its shareholders. The amount of the
bonus not to exceed Ten (10) days' pay.

DISMISSAL
(3) The Company agrees not to dismiss from its employ
any workman without just cause. To make the definition of
"just cause" thoroughly understood, the Company reserves to
itself the right to discharge workmen for any of the follow-
ing causes:-
1. Continued depression in trade.
2. Reduction of number of workmen due to re-arrangement
of the Company's plants.
3. Insubordination.
4. Theft or dishonesty.
5. Inattention to duty.
6. Continued bad daily timekeeping.
7. Continued or malicious breach of the Company's
general rules.

SUSPENSION
(4) Workmen in time of slackness will be suspended as
in the opinion of the Company is requisite, but the Company
guarantees employment to workmen for a minimum of twelve
(12) days in each twenty-eight (28) days, and should the
depression become protracted, the Company reserves the right
to pay off certain workmen. Should it be necessary to do
so, the Company will pay to such men:

GRIEVANCES
(12) It must be clearly understood that any legitimate

new representatives' signatures must be submitted and attached

On November 27, mediation was conducted by
Mr. P.Y. KOO of the Industrial Section of the S.M.C.
in connection with the demands submitted by workers
of the Shanghai Dockyards, 640 Yangtszepoo Road, and
discussions will continue to-day.

It is reported that a number of employees of
the Dockyards are dissatisfied with the Eastern
District Branch of the Chinese Labourers' Welfare
Association, 127 Rangoon Road, for its failure to
secure the immediate release of a worker arrested
by the Municipal Police on the outbreak of the strike.
On November 27, a fight took place between a worker
and a labour representative in the premises of the
Dockyards following an altercation over the activities
of the Eastern District Branch of the Chinese
Labourers' Welfare Association. The labour
representative was of the opinion that the Branch
has failed to convince the workers in respect of
its power in bringing about successful results for
workers involved in labour disputes.

McKeown

11月27日，工部局工业科的顾（音译）先生就杨树浦路640号上海船坞工人提出的要求进行了调解，讨论将于今日继续进行。
