Yulin Road Police    325/41.

Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards, 640
Yangtszepoo Road.

Sir,

At 3 p.m. 14-11-41, a telephone message was
received from Mr. I. Beattie, manager of the Shanghai
Dockyards, 640 Yangtszepoo Road, reporting having some
trouble with his workers.

C.D.S. 235 were thereupon enquired, and
ascertained that the workers, numbering approximately
1,300 fitters, blacksmiths and coolies etc, had con-
gregated outside the office of the above address, and
demanded a 50% increase in wages and allowances.

The management refused to enter into negotiations
with the workers until they returned to work. The
workers refused, finally leaving the premises, at
5 p.m. 14-11-41 without any untoward incidents occurring.

In the meantime the management had posted on
the factory gate, the following notice: "On the 6-11-41
representatives of the workers discussed with the manage-
ment, a demand for an increase of wages. However as
the price of commodities are now unsettled, but likely
to decrease in the near future, because of S.M.C.
control, the management will not increase wages until
the commodity prices become stable. Should the prices
however, continue to rise, an increase of wages will
be granted as from 5-11-41, and should the prices
decrease, the present wage standard will remain."

D.S. 143.

Sen. Det. i/c.

TRANSLATION

NOTICE

November 14, 1941.

With reference to the demands submitted to the
management by the foremen representing the workers, we
hereby make an announcement as follows:-

On November 6, when holding a meeting with the
management, the foremen brought up for discussion the
demands of the workers for wage increases. The
management promised to consider the demands, but, owing
to the difficulty in formulating measures at that time
when the prices of commodities were changing rapidly,
they requested the labour representatives to wait for
some time pending the result of the efforts which were
being made by the S.M.C. in suppressing hoarding and
profiteering by Chinese and other nationals.

The management hereby make an assurance that
whatever readjustment measures are decided upon in
future they shall be retroactive from November 5, the
date of submitting the demands. The workers therefore
will not suffer any loss for the period of waiting for
a settlement. The management also wish to assure the
workers that a decision regarding this matter will be
made as soon as the prices of food and other commodities
have shown tendencies of stabilization.

Although the cost of living has dropped slightly
during this period of negotiations, the management are
paying the workers according to the existing scales and
are refraining from making any changes for the time being.
It is expected that the local market will soon reach
an agreeable stage and in this event further meetings
of both parties will be convened in a few days for joint

通告

一九四一年十一月十四日。

兹就工头代表工人向资方提出的要求，公告如下：

十一月六日，工头在与资方举行会议时，提出了工人增加工资的要求以供讨论。资方承诺考虑这些要求，但由于当时物价变动迅速，难以制定具体措施，故请劳工代表稍候片刻，以待上海公共租界工部局在遏制华人及其他国籍人士囤积居奇和牟取暴利方面所作努力的结果。

资方特此保证，今后无论决定采取何种调整措施，均将追溯至提出要求之日，即十一月五日起生效。因此，工人在等待解决期间不会遭受任何损失。资方还希望向工人保证，一旦食品和其他商品的价格显示出稳定趋势，将立即就此事项作出决定。

尽管在此谈判期间生活费用略有下降，但资方仍按现行标准向工人支付工资，并暂时不作任何变更。预计本地市场很快将达到一个令人满意的阶段，届时双方将在数日内再次召开会议，共同

Resumption of work by employees of Ah Yang General Contractor,
No. 9, Jansen Road.

L.S. Pascoe

Sir,

At 7 a.m. 16-5-41, twenty employees of the above
general contractor, resumed work, at the daily rate
of $6.00, this representing an increase of $1.00 per
day.

At 7 a.m. 19-5-41, a further one hundred workers
appeared for work at the dockyards and have resumed
work on the above basis.

The workers went back to work against the wishes
of the Transport Union who had asked for at least an
increase of $1.50 per day.

It is understood that the remainder of the strikers
are also desirous of returning to work, but at present,
their services are not required.

Date May 11th., 41.

2nd.

Continued Strike by Employees of Ah Yang General Contractor,
No. 9, Jansen Road.

D.S. 143 Pascoe.

Sir,

Further enquiries have been made at the Shanghai
Dockyards, 640 Yangtzepoo Road, and when it was ascer-
tained, that the three hundred strikers are still out.
The workers did appear for work on the 9-5-41, under
the impression they had been promised an increase of $1.50
per day. On learning of their mistake, they then approach-
ed the management of the Dockyards, who however, informed
the strikers that the wage question was a matter for the
contractors. The matter is now believed to have
concerned the contractors, and whereas some of the
contractors involved, wished to give the $1.50 increase,
the majority vetoed it.

It has also been learned that approximately one hun-
dred and fifty coolies have been employed by outside con-
tractors, and are now performing the work of the strikers
at $6.50 - $7.00 per day.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

Sgt. Det. i/c.
D.D.U. "D" Div.

侦探警士 143号 帕斯科（Pascoe）。

先生：

经在杨树浦路640号上海船坞进一步调查，查明三百名罢工工人目前仍处于罢工状态。工人们曾于1941年5月9日到岗上班，因误以为已获承诺每日加薪1.50元。在得知系误解后，他们随即接洽船坞管理层，但管理层告知罢工者，工资问题属承包商事宜。据信此事确系承包商之间的问题，尽管部分涉事承包商愿意给予1.50元的加薪，但大多数承包商予以否决。

另获悉，外部承包商已雇佣约一百五十名苦力，目前正以每日6.50至7.00元的工资从事原罢工工人的工作。

Yulin Road. 8941 A
May 7th, 5-41

Strike By Temporary Workers of Ah Yang General Contractor,
No. 9 Jansen Road.
D.S. 143 Pascoe.

Sir,

At 8.30 a.m. 7-5-41, a telephone message was received from Mr. L. Beattle of the Shanghai Dockyards 640 Yangtsepor Road, reporting having trouble with some of their temporary contracted workfols.

C.D.C. 262 and the undersigned attended, and ascertained that at 7 a.m. 6-5-41, approximately three hundred ship chippers and scrappers, had gone on strike. These workers, however, are not directly employed by the Shanghai Dockyards, but by a contractor, one named Ah Yang, No. 9 Jansen Road, to whom a demand for an increase of pay, from the present rate of $5.00, to $7.00 was made on the 5- -41.

On meeting with a refusal they declared a strike, and did not attend work on the 6-5-41.

In the meantime, the Shanghai Dockyards wishing to urgently finish one of the ships lying in drydock, persuaded about forty of their painters to do the work of scrapping. On finishing the scrapping, the painters could then proceed with their normal occupation, of finishing the job, by painting.

The chippers and scrappers heard of this plan, and at about 8 a.m. 7th inst a large number arrived outside the maingate of the abovementioned dockyards. They then threatened the painters with dire results, should they continue. The painters refused from further scrapping, and the strikers departed.

杨森路9号阿阳（Ah Yang，音译）总承包商临时工罢工案。
警员编号 143 帕斯科（Pascoe）。

先生：

1941年5月7日上午8时30分，接扬子江路640号上海船坞公司 L. Beattle（音译）先生电话报告，称其部分临时承包工人引发纠纷。

刑事侦缉处警员编号 262 及本人随即前往现场，经查实，1941年5月6日上午7时，约三百名船舶铲锈工和除锈工举行罢工。然而，这些工人并非由上海船坞公司直接雇佣，而是受雇于一名名为阿阳（Ah Yang，音译）的承包商，其地址为杨森路9号。该承包商于1941年5月5日收到工人要求将工资从目前的5.00元提高至7.00元的诉求。

因遭拒绝，工人宣布罢工，并于1941年5月6日未出勤。

其间，上海船坞公司急于完成一艘停在干船坞内的船舶工程，遂说服约四十名油漆工从事除锈工作。待除锈工作完成后，油漆工即可继续其本职工作，即进行油漆涂装。

铲锈工和除锈工获悉此计划后，于本月7日上午8时许，大批人员抵达上述船坞的大门外。他们威胁油漆工，若继续工作将面临严重后果。油漆工因此拒绝继续除锈，罢工者随后离去。

Made by D.S.I. Ross. Forwarded by Junzo S / P O/C

Sir,

At 7.40 a.m. June 22nd 1940, F.S. 334 Kay telephon-
ed to Yulin Road Station to the effect that employees at
the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtzepoo Road, had
ceased work to enforce a demand for increased wages.

Detectives visited the scene, and enquiries ascer-
tained that at about 7 a.m. June 22nd 1940, some 350
workers employed in the capacity of painters and strippers
had ceased work in an attempt to enforce a demand for
increase of $1.00 per day in wages.

The strikers are employed through the agency of
contractors, and are at the present time in receipt of
a daily wage of $2.50. A few days ago they requested the
contractors to increase their wages, and the increase
not being forthcoming they ceased work.

At 8 a.m. June 22nd 1940, the strikers dispersed,
and no untoward incident occurred.

The workers employed by the management of the
Dockyards are not affected up to the present time.

Police have been detailed for duty at the scene to
prevent possible acts of intimidation.

Special Branch informed.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
（签名）

Made by D.S.I. Ross. Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Sir,

At 10 a.m. June 7th 1940, Mr. J.A.Bonnyman,
Manager, The Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtzepoo
Road, telephoned Yulin Road Station and requested the
attendance of a detective in connection with unrest
existing among the Chinese workers of the company.

In response to this message the undersigned
interviewed Mr. Bonnyman, who stated, that he had
received information from a reliable source in Shanghai
which could be considered practically official, to the
effect that agents of the Wong Ching Wei regime were
taking an active interest in the labour situation in
the company, and that further trouble was to be expect-
ed on June 15th 1940.

It was also learned from Mr. J.C.Amour, Assistant
Manager, that the workers whom the company dismissed
following the recent strike, some 250 in number, were
intimidating the re-employed workers, and endeavouring
to force them to pay ten days wages to each of the
dismissed employees. Mr. Amour emphasized that this
question of payment to the dismissed workers was a
private affair, and the company did not wish to become
involved in the matter.

Efforts were made to elicit from Mr. Bonnyman
the source of his information, regarding agents of
Wong Ching Wei taking an interest in the affairs of
the Company, but the gentleman was not in the least
enlightening on the subject.

为回应此消息，具名者会见了 Bonnyman 先生，他称，他从上海一个可被视为近乎官方的可靠来源获悉，汪精卫政权的特工正积极关注该公司的劳工局势，且预计1940年6月15日将发生进一步的麻烦。

另从副经理 J.C. Amour 先生处得知，在最近的罢工后被公司解雇的约250名工人，正在恐吓被重新雇用的工人，并企图强迫他们向每名被解雇员工支付十天工资。Amour 先生强调，向被解雇工人付款一事属于私人事务，公司不希望卷入其中。

Notice posted outside Country HouseNotice posted outside Country House, off Jansen Road.

Fellow-workers! We must have prestige. We must not
act as "running-dogs" for foreigners, as Dong Miao Ts
(董妙慈), the traitor, who returned to work today. He only
stayed with us for one week. He is not our friend. Money
is his God. He also received bribes from the workers, and if
the bribe was not forthcoming, he would speak evilly of the
man to the foreigners. Do you know where his property comes
from? Most of it was bought by bribes received from us.
Formerly on the occasion of each festival, he would demand
that we give to him the sum of at least 20.00 each, as a
gift.

When the present strike commenced, owing to the High
Cost of Living, we submitted demands to the management for
increased wages. Our actions were opposed by Dong Miao Ts,
who stopped us from doing so, and has caused many workers to
be dismissed, especially those who failed to give him gifts
in the past. He alone can now steal property from the Company,
and dispose of it as he wishes. He has caused the dismissal of
more than 1,000 workmen, of whom over 200 cannot maintain a
living.

If he ever comes to our place we will not excuse him,
but will show him our power and will not let him return. He
should prepare his coffin, as he will surely be dead at an
early date. He has enjoyed much pleasure in this world, but
he will be repaid in the next.

It will be noticed that the "running-dog" of Dong Miao
Ts is Jung Ping Kong (陳炳光) or Hsu Ah Kong (許阿光), who will
return to work with him.

Whoever shall tear down this notice is a "Running-dog"
of Dong Miao Ts.
page_data.zh:
张贴在乡间别墅外的告示张贴在詹森路（Jansen Road）旁乡间别墅外的告示。

工友们！我们必须有威望。我们绝不能像董妙慈（Dong Miao Ts）那个叛徒那样，充当外国人的“走狗”，他今天已复工。他只在我们这里待了一个星期。他不是我们的朋友。金钱是他的上帝。他还收受工人的贿赂，如果贿赂不到位，他就会向外国人讲那人的坏话。你们知道他的财产是从哪里来的吗？大部分是用从我们这里收受的贿赂购买的。以前每逢节日，他都会要求我们每人至少给他20.00元作为礼物。

当此次罢工因生活费用高昂而开始时，我们向管理层提出了增加工资的要求。我们的行动遭到了董妙慈的反对，他阻止我们这样做，并导致许多工人被解雇，尤其是那些过去未给他送礼的人。现在只有他能从公司窃取财产，并随意处置。他导致一千多名工人被解雇，其中二百多人无法维持生计。

如果他再来我们这里，我们绝不宽恕他，而要向他展示我们的力量，不让他回去。他应该准备好棺材，因为他肯定会早死。他在今世享尽了乐，但来世必将得到报应。

值得注意的是，董妙慈的“走狗”是陈炳光（Jung Ping Kong）或许阿光（Hsu Ah Kong），他们将与他一同复工。

凡撕毁此告示者，即是董妙慈的“走狗”。

Subject Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtszepoo Road.

Made by. D.S.I. Ross Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,

The strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640,
Yangtszepoo Road, continues this morning, April 30th,
1940.

No untoward incident was reported during April
29th 1940.

During the afternoon of April 29th 1940, Mr. P.Y.Koo,
S.M.C./Industrial Section, contacted some of the strikers
and acted as an intermediary between them and the manage-
ment.

Mr. Koo succeeded in separating the workers into two
groups, i.e. (1) Workmen whom the management desire to
re-engage, and (2) Workmen whom the management refuse to
re-employ.

New demands were submitted by the two groups, and
replies given by the management, as follows:-
Group No. 1 (Workmen).
(1) The company shall recognize that the Labour Union
has the right to represent the workmen of the
Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., including the coolies.
(2) Increase of 30% in wages be granted.
(3) Wages and Rice Allowance during the strike should
be paid.

The management gave the following reply to these
demands.
(1) The company recognizes the Labour Union of the
Workmen, but not including the coolies.
The coolies shall enjoy 75% of the privileges
provided in the Agreement instead of 66% as
formerly.

Sir,

The strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640,
Yangtszepoo Road, continues this morning (April 27th 1940).
No untoward incident occurred during the course of
April 26th 1940.

The lodahs and crews of the launches operated by
the Company resumed work during the morning of April
26th 1940.

At 2 p.m. April 26th 1940, some 200 to 300 of the
strikers held a meeting at the country house off Yang-
tszepoo Road, to discuss the present strike situation.
The men agreed to return to work immediately if the
management would re-engage all the strikers, but failure
to do so would result in the strike being continued. It
was also agreed to approach three former representatives
named Lee Foh Sung (李福生), Dong Miau Tsze (唐妙子) and
Woo Soong Ling (吴松林), and request them to intercede

Sir,

The strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640,
Yangtsepoo Road, continues this morning, April 26th
1940.

No untoward incident was reported during the
course of April 25th 1940.

On the morning of April 25th 1940, the management
of the Dockyards posted a notice containing a list of
all employees whom the company desire to re-engage,
and calling upon these workmen to register within the
period of seven days, or forfeit all privileges previously enjoyed.

The list contains the numbers of some six hundred
odd workers, which is some three hundred short of the
number employed prior to the strike.

The Special Branch is already in possession of a
copy of the notice and a list of the numbers of the
workmen.

In connection with the re-employment of these
workers, the strikers have posted a notice outside the
entrance to the country house, off Yangtsepoo Road,
which they use as a headquarters, calling a meeting of
the strikers between 2 p.m. and 3 p.m. April 26th 1940,
on the vacant piece of ground at Jansen and Yangtsepoo
Roads corner, to discuss this latest development.

30th REPORT
Date May 1st., 19 40
Subject Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtsepoo Road.
Made by D. S. I. Ross Forwarded by [Signature] Supt.

Sir,

The strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640,
Yangtsepoo Road, continues this morning, May 1st. 1940.
No untoward incident was reported during the
course of April 30th. 1940.

Mr. P. Y. Koo, S.M.C. Industrial Section, continued
his negotiations with the management and the strikers,
and, during the afternoon of April 30th. 1940, succeeded
in reaching a settlement with the body of strikers whom
the management did not desire to further employ (some 250
in number).

The terms of the settlement are as follows:-
(1) The dismissed workers will be divided into
three groups.
(2) Group No. 1, consisting of 10% of the strikers
whom it was proposed to dismiss, will be re-
employed by the Company.
(3) Group No. 2, consisting of 30% of the same
strikers, will be paid a Discharge Allowance
in accordance with the terms of the agreement
under which they were employed prior to the
strike, and will be given preferential treatment
when occasion arises to engage workers in the
future.
(4) Group No. 3, consisting of 60% of the strikers
in the same category, will be permanently
dismissed. They will be paid a Discharge
Allowance of 25 days' pay for each three years
of service with the Company.

Sir,
The strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640,
Yangtszepoo Road, continues this morning, April 29th
1940.
No untoward incident was reported over the week-
end.
At 9.30 a.m. April 28th 1940, some 250 strikers
held a meeting at the Country House which they are
using as a Headquarters, off Yangtszepoo Road near
Jansen Road, and discussed the present position.
During the course of the meeting the majority
of those present expressed dissatisfaction with the
leadership of Fitter No. 115 Yih Mao Cao (葉毛草),
and on a number of occasions bodily harm was threatened
the man.
One of the delegates named Zung Ping Kong (陳炳庚)
resigned his position. He was arrested by the French
Police on April 23rd 1940, and informed the meeting
that he has suffered sufficient in the interest of the
cause.
Before the meeting terminated the strikers selected
three foremen and former representatives named Lee Foh
Sung (李福生), Dong Miau Tsze (唐妙子), and Woo Soong
Ling (吳松林), also a fitter named Zung Liang (陳良),
and instructed that they visit the Special Branch,
Police Headquarters, on the morning of April 29th 1940,
and request Det. Sub. Insp. Kao, to intercede with the
management on their behalf.
These delegates have been instructed to request

Subject Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtszepoo Road.

Made by D.S.I. Ross Forwarded by [签名] Insp.

Sir,

The workers of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640,
Yangtszepoo Road, remained on strike this morning (24-4-
1940).

The majority of the employees of the International
and Tung-Ka-Doo Docks, branches in Pootung, have resumed
work, and the situation at these two docks is practi-
cally normal.

The management have arranged to commence work on a
Japanese ship which they expect to tie up alongside the
Dockyards, during the afternoon of the 24-4-1940.

Mr. Bonnyman, manager of the Dockyards, is contem-
plating posting a list of workers whom the company
desire to re-engage, and giving a time limit of one week
during which these employees can register, failure to
do so during the stated period to result in the forfeit
of all privileges previously enjoyed.

Yangtsepoo Road, continues this morning, April 18th

The workers at the company's dockyard at Tung-Ka-Doo
ceased work on April 17th 1940, apparently in sympathy
with the strikers.

It has been learned by C.I.S. 235 that Fitter No. 116

Subject. Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtsepoo Road.

Made by. D.S.I. Ross Forwarded by （签名）

Sir,

The strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd.,
640, Yangtsepoo Road, continued this morning, April
17th., 1940.

At about 9 a.m. April 16th., 1940, some one
hundred and fifty of the strikers, led by Fitter
No. 116 Yee Mao Dao (叶茂道), visited the International
Dock, Pootung, under the same ownership, and intimidated
the workers therein employed into joining in the
strike.

According to the management of the Company,
Fitter No. 116 Yee Mao Dao was successful in obtaining
the assistance of one named Foo Ching Sung (Chinese
characters not available), the Chief of the Yang
Ching (洋泾) Village, Pootung, in this new development.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
（签名 J.S. Ross）

strikers approached Mr. C.A. Momber, a former manager

10th. REPORT
Subject Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtsepoo Road.
Made by I. I. Ross Forwarded by ________________

Sir,

The strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd.,
640, Yangtsepoo Road, continued on April 4th., 1940.

At 12 noon April 4th., 1940, ten of the delegates
of the strikers visited the Dockyards and notified
the management that they had resigned their positions
as representatives of the strikers, owing to their
inability to negotiate such a settlement of the
dispute as would be acceptable to the workers.

In the afternoon of April 4th., 1940, the
management of the Dockyards posted a notice outside
the entrance to the premises, to the effect that
**〔此处转录不清〕**
would be no further new hands employed to replace
them. The notice also gave warning that the grants
**〔此处转录不清〕**
increase of 10% would not apply to any new men.
A detailed translation of the notice is in
possession of the Special Branch.

At 6 p.m. April 4th 1940, S.D.S. obtained
information to the effect that the strikers intended
to hold a meeting at 9 a.m. April 5th 1940, at a
country house at Lamson Co. and Yangtsepoo Road
corner, to consider future action.

The Special Branch was informed regarding the
proposed meeting.

All due precautions have been adopted by Officer
i/c, Yulin Road Station.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
J. Ross
D.S.I.

6th REPORT
Date March 27th, 1940.
Subject. Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards, 640, Yangtszepoo Road.
Made by. T.M.L. Ross Forwarded by [Signature]
Sir,
The strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640,
Yangtszepoo Road, continued on March 27th 1940.
At 9.30 a.m. March 27th 1940, the management paid
to the strikers outstanding wages. Some 596 workers
attended and received payment, but some 140 odd failed
to attend. The usual police precautions were adopted,
and no untoward incident occurred.
At 10 a.m. March 27th 1940, the management of the
company received a number of the strikers delegates, and
handed to them a written reply to the demands submitted,
in which was also expressed the views of the management
on the strike and the events leading thereto. A copy
of this reply, written in Chinese, was obtained from
the management, and has been submitted to the Special
Branch for favour of translation.
（批：S.W. 27/3 27/7）
The management of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd.,
have received certain information to the effect that
Coolie No. 112 Lee Tsung Kwei (李增贵) is the leader
of a band of strikers which is engaged in intimidating
employees who prefer to resume work. Efforts are now
being made to apprehend this coolie, for questioning.
I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
[Signature]
D.D.C. "D"

阁下：

位于杨树浦路640号的上海船坞有限公司（Shanghai Dockyards Ltd.）的罢工事件在1940年3月27日仍在继续。

1940年3月27日上午9时30分，资方向罢工工人支付了拖欠的工资。约有596名工人到场并领取了工资，但仍有约140余人未到场。警方采取了常规的预防措施，未发生任何意外事件。

1940年3月27日上午10时，公司管理层接见了一批罢工工人代表，并向他们递交了一份针对所提要求的书面答复，其中也表达了管理层对此次罢工及导致罢工事件的看法。该中文答复的副本已从资方获取，并已提交至特别科（Special Branch）以便翻译。
（批注：S.W. 3月27日 / 7月27日）

上海船坞有限公司管理层收到某些情报，称苦力第112号李增贵（Lee Tsung Kwei）是一伙罢工者的头目，该伙人正从事恐吓那些愿意复工的员工的活动。目前正设法逮捕该名苦力，以进行讯问。

Sir,

On the afternoon of March 23rd., 1940, representatives
of the strikers had a further meeting with the manage-

on March 25th., 1940. D.S.I. Logan and D.S.I. Yao, attached

and P.C. 788 brought to Yulin Road Station one
named Lang Ching Yue (梁清月) 42, Tsingkiang, 110, Yang
an Li, Yangtsepoo Road, one of the strikers, in
connection with an attempt which he made to prevent
workers from collecting wages.

was found impossible to obtain evidence to prove
a charge of "Attempted Intimidation". He was permitted
to go, after detectives attached to the Special Branch
had also questioned him.

Subject Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtsepoo Road.
Made by D.S.I. Ross. Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Sir,
At 1.30 p.m. 14/3/1940, a telephone message was received at Yulin Road Station from a Russian watchman, employed by the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtsepoo Road, to the effect that the management expected trouble during the afternoon.
Detectives attended the premises, and found that the greater majority of the workers were attending a meeting to discuss better conditions for the employees, and failed to resume work.
The Special Branch was notified, and Supt. Mason, D.S.I. Logan, and D.S.I. Kao attended with a view to ascertaining the nature of the trouble, and the possibility of arranging a settlement.
The employees failed to resume work following the tiffin interval, so the company engaged a number of Russian employees to assist the foreign staff to float the s.s. "Fernmoor", then in dry-dock for repairs.
At 3.30 p.m. 14/3/1940, a further telephone message was received to the effect that a riot was in progress at the Dockyards.
A party of Police, with Insp. Brownrigg i/c., immediately proceeded to the scene.
Upon arrival it was learned that the strikers had attacked the foreigners and the Russian employees when an attempt was made to float the ship.
As a result of the fight which ensued, the following foreigners sustained injury:-

先生：
1940 年 3 月 14 日下午 1 时 30 分，榆林路捕房接到杨树浦路 640 号上海船坞有限公司一名俄籍更夫的电话留言，称管理层预计下午会发生骚乱。
侦探随即前往该处所，发现绝大多数工人正在开会，讨论改善雇员待遇事宜，并未复工。
警方已通知特别支部，梅森警司（Supt. Mason）、侦探副督察洛根（D.S.I. Logan）及侦探副督察高（D.S.I. Kao）随即到场，旨在查明骚乱性质，并探讨达成和解的可能性。
午膳间歇后，雇员仍未复工，因此公司雇用了一批俄籍员工，协助外籍职员将当时正停在干船坞内修理的“芬莫尔”号（s.s. "Fernmoor"）轮船浮起。
1940 年 3 月 14 日下午 3 时 30 分，又接到电话留言，称船坞内正在发生暴动。
由布朗里格巡官（Insp. Brownrigg）率领的一队警员立即赶赴现场。
抵达后获悉，当试图将轮船浮起时，罢工者袭击了外籍人员及俄籍员工。
在随后的斗殴中，下列外籍人员受伤：-

Subject Twenty-One Coolies Suspended Employment At The Shanghai
Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtsepoo Road.
Made by J.I. Ross. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

On the 27-2-1940, the management of the Shanghai
Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtsepoo Road, suspended ten
carrying coolies, owing to slackness of work.

A further eleven coolies are under notice to
cease work on the night of the 1-3-1940, for a similar
reason.

The ten coolies who were suspended on the 27-2-1940,
refused to collect the wages due to them.

In the meantime, they approached a foreman, named
Fah Lau Nyi (樊老二), and insisted that he should
approach the management on their behalf, and enter a
demand for the payment of twenty-five days wages, in
lieu of notice.

It is the custom in the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd.,
to pay a bonus to employees who are discharged owing
to slackness of work, but due to the fact that these
coolies have not been discharged they are not considered
to be eligible for the bonus.

The foreman, Fah Lau Nyi, refused to approach the
management in connection with the demand, and this
resulted in four of the coolies attacking him inside
the Dockyards, at about 1.30 p.m. 29-2-1940. The fore-
man sustained slight injury, and was discharged from
hospital following treatment.

Detectives attended and took the four coolies
responsible for the assault into custody. They are
(1) Wong Sung Kung (王生根), (2) Pan Soo Siang (潘寿祥),
(3) Pan Yang Mau (潘楊毛), and (4) Pau Zung Kung (乾正根)

敬启者：

1940年2月27日，位于杨树浦路640号的上海船坞有限公司管理层因工作清淡，暂停了十名搬运苦力的工作。

另有十一名苦力接到通知，出于同样原因，将于1940年3月1日晚停止工作。

1940年2月27日被暂停工作的十名苦力拒绝领取应得工资。

其间，他们找到一名名叫樊老二（Fah Lau Nyi）的工头，坚持要求他代表他们向管理层交涉，并提出支付二十五天工资以代替通知期的要求。

上海船坞有限公司的惯例是，向因工作清淡而被解雇的员工发放奖金，但由于这些苦力并未被解雇，故被认为不符合领取奖金的资格。

工头樊老二拒绝就该项要求与管理层交涉，导致四名苦力于1940年2月29日下午约1时30分在船坞内袭击了他。该工头受轻伤，经治疗后出院。

侦探到场并将涉嫌袭击的四名苦力拘捕。他们是：(1) 王生根（Wong Sung Kung），(2) 潘寿祥（Pan Soo Siang），(3) 潘楊毛（Pan Yang Mau），以及 (4) 乾正根（Pau Zung Kung）。

Date December 1st, 1939.

Subject. Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640 Yangtszepoo Road.

Made by. D.S.I. ROSS        Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,
    Between 4.30 p.m. and 6.30 p.m. November 30th 1939, a further meeting was held between the management of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., and representatives of workers and dismissed workers.
    The most important question under discussion was the subject of the gratuity to be paid to the dismissed workers, as the workers now operating refuse to sign the new agreement pending settlement of this point.
    It was eventually agreed by the management and the two parties concerned that a gratuity of $5.00 be paid to the dismissed workers for each year of service. This decision means that the management will have to pay the thirty-four workers sums ranging from $75.00 to $180.00.
    Arrangements have been made to pay these gratuities at 4 p.m. December 1st 1939, at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., and the usual police precautions will be maintained.
    In connection with the new agreement negotiated between the management and the present workers, the last outstanding point in this connection was also discussed and settled when the management agreed to pay an annual bonus equivalent to one week's pay to every worker, at Chinese New Year.
    The meeting was attended by Mr. P.Y. Koo, S.M.C./Industrial Section, C.D.S. 281 of the Special Branch, and C.D.S. 235 attached to Yulin Road Station.
    On November 30th 1939, the situation at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., was normal, and following the successful conclusion of the negotiations no further trouble is anticipated.

D.D.O."D" .

    讨论的最重要议题是向被解雇工人支付遣散费的问题，因为目前在职的工人拒绝签署新协议，直至该问题得到解决。
    最终，管理层与有关双方达成协议，向被解雇工人按每服务一年支付5.00美元的标准发放遣散费。这一决定意味着管理层须向三十四名工人支付金额在75.00美元至180.00美元不等的款项。
    已安排于1939年12月1日下午4时在上海船坞有限公司支付上述遣散费，并将维持常规的警务预防措施。
    关于管理层与现职工人之间协商的新协议，与此相关的最后一个悬而未决的问题也在此次会议上得到讨论和解决，即管理层同意在农历新年期间向每位工人支付相当于一周薪水的年终奖金。
    出席会议的有：工部局工业科 P.Y. Koo 先生、特务处警探编号281，以及派驻榆林路捕房的特务处警探编号235。

Sir,

The Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., continued to operate normally during November 29th 1939.

At 4 p.m., the same day, the management and representatives of the workers again met on the premises of the company. A written agreement of working conditions was prepared, and agreed to by both parties, but the representatives of the workers refused to affix their signature pending the settlement of the dispute with the thirty-four dismissed employees.

The management held a further meeting, at which six representatives of the dismissed employees were present, & offered to them a fixed scale of bonuses. The dismissed employees refused the amounts offered, and demanded sums much in excess. The meeting was finally adjourned to the afternoon of November 30th 1939.

Sir,

On November 27th., 1939, with the exception of twenty employees the Shanghai Dockyards had a full complement at work.

At 5.30 p.m. November 27th., 1939, Mr. J. C. Armour and Mr. L. Beattie, representing the management, met representatives of the workers, and discussed terms for the settlement of the strike. The conference progressed favourably, and was adjourned to the afternoon of November 28th., 1939, when it is believed that a settlement will be reached.

Mr. P. Y. Koo, Inspector of the Industrial Section of the S.M.C., and C.D.S. 235 attached to Yulin Road Station, were present during the negotiations, and will also attend on November 28th., 1939.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

INDUSTRIAL DISPUTE

The strike of some 1,700 workers employed by
the Shanghai Dockyards, 640 Yangtszepoo Road continues
to-day, November 24, 1939.

I called on Mr. J. D. Armour at the Shanghai
Dockyards this morning. It was reported that some 800
workers have registered in the Chinese Workers' Welfare
Association, 127 Rangoon Road, and a small group asking
the Chinese Republic Workers' League at Yootung for sup-
port.

The Industrial Section representative was
requested by workers to see them at the Chinese Workers'
Welfare Association to arrange the time for negotiation
with the management. I met the Chief of Eastern Shanghai
Branch of the Chinese Workers' Welfare Association, Mr.
Moh Ling Tsang (莫林章), and a group of workers of the
Shanghai Dockyards at 127 Rangoon Road at 12 O'clock this
noon. It was arranged that the workers will appoint their
representatives and bring their demands to the management
at 3 p.m. for negotiation.

No workers' representation appeared at the time
as it was arranged. It was reported that the workers were
not able to appoint formal representatives and to agree
on the demands to be submitted to the management. They
requested to postpone the meeting at 10:30 a.m. to-morrow
morning, November 25, 1939.

November 25, 1939.

Foreman Lee Poh Seng telephoned to the Industrial
Section this morning indicating no agreement on workers'
representation had been reached last night. The dismissed
coolies are demanding that mediation be conducted by the
Special Service of the Japanese Naval Landing Party; but
regular workers desire the services of the Industrial Section.

G. S. Sd.

劳资纠纷

受雇于杨树浦路640号上海船坞有限公司的约1,700名工人的罢工行动持续至今日，即1939年11月24日。

本人今晨前往上海船坞有限公司拜访了J. D. Armour先生。据报，约有800名工人已在兰路127号的中国劳工福利会登记，另有一小群人向位于浦东的中华民国工人联盟寻求支持。

工人们请求工业科代表前往中国劳工福利会与他们会面，以安排与管理层进行谈判的时间。本人于今日中午12时在兰路127号会见了中国劳工福利会沪东分会主任莫林章先生（Moh Ling Tsang）及一群上海船坞有限公司的工人。会上商定，工人将推选代表，并于下午3时向管理层提出诉求进行谈判。

届时并无工人代表按约定出现。据报，工人未能推选出正式代表，也未能就向管理层提交的诉求达成一致。他们请求将会议推迟至明日上午，即1939年11月25日上午10时30分举行。

1939年11月25日。

领班李宝生（Lee Poh Seng，音译）今晨致电工业科，表示昨晚未能就工人代表人选达成协议。被解雇的苦力要求由日本海军陆战队特务机关进行调解；但正式工人则希望由工业科提供服务。

Made by D. S. I. Ross. Forwarded by Supt. Inspector. J. Tung

Sir,

At 10 a.m. November 25th 1939, eight representatives of the strikers attended the office of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtszepoo Road, and held a discussion with the management. During this discussion, which was conducted in the presence of Mr. P. Y. Koo, Inspector of the Industrial Section of the S.M.C., C.D.S. 291 attached to the Special Branch, and C.D.S 835 attached to Yulin Road Station, the representatives tabled fourteen demands. A translation copy of these are attached.

The management agreed to give sympathetic consideration to the demands, but informed the representatives that they could not discuss these before Monday, November 27th 1939.

The Company, however, agreed to the 12th demand, i.e., the payment of wages during the stoppage, if the workers -less the thirty-four dismissed- resumed employment immediately and continued during the period of mediation. The representatives stated that they were not empowered to agree to this condition. However, at the behest of Mr. Koo and the detectives, they agreed to call a meeting of the strikers during the afternoon, and ascertain their views on the subject.

At 3 p.m. November 25th 1939, the representatives met the employees in Room No. 15, the Doong An ( 同安 ) Lodging House, Lane 122, House 8, Thorburn Road. After a lengthy discussion, during which Mr. Koo and the detectives urged the men to resume work during the

敬启者：

1939 年 11 月 25 日上午 10 时，八名罢工代表前往位于杨树浦路 640 号的上海船坞有限公司办公室，与管理层举行会谈。此次讨论在工部局工业科督察顾 P. Y. 先生（Mr. P. Y. Koo）、附属于特务科的侦探 C.D.S. 291 以及附属于榆林路捕房的侦探 C.D.S. 835 的在场见证下进行，期间代表们提出了十四项要求。这些要求的译本附后。

管理层同意对这些要求给予同情性的考虑，但告知代表们，在 1939 年 11 月 27 日（星期一）之前无法就此进行讨论。

然而，公司方面同意了第 12 项要求，即在停工期间支付工资，前提是工人——除被解雇的三十四人外——立即复工，并在调解期间继续工作。代表们表示，他们无权同意这一条件。不过，应顾先生及侦探们的要求，他们同意在当天下午召开罢工工人会议，以征询大家对此事的意见。

1939 年 11 月 25 日下午 3 时，代表们在韬宾路（Thorburn Road）122 弄 8 号同安旅舍（Doong An Lodging House）15 号房间与工人们会面。经过长时间的讨论，期间顾先生和侦探们敦促工人在

Translation of Fourteen Demands Submitted by
the Strikers of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd.,
640, Yangtszepoo Road.

1. The permanent employees of the Company will not be liable
to dismissal without sufficient cause.
2. The thirty-four dismissed employees be re-instated, and the
employees dismissed following the outbreak of the Sino-
Japanese Hostilities should have right to seek re-
engagement.
3. If the Company intends to dismiss employees owing to
slackness, the system of alternative shifts should be
commenced, but each employee should be given at least
eighteen days work in every twenty-eight days (night
duty not to be included). Employees who are dismissed,
owing to slackness of work, should be granted bonus of
one month's salary for each year's employment.
4. Employees are to be granted at least eight day's holiday
every year, and to be paid. If the employee continues
to work during the holiday double wages should be
granted. Payment should also be made for holiday's since
the beginning of the Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
5. At Chinese New Year, each employee should be granted a bonus
of two weeks' wages.
6. If the employee is injured during the course of employment,
the Company should accept responsibility for the payment
of medical and hospital expenses. If the employee is
page_data.zh:
杨树浦路640号上海船坞有限公司罢工工人所提十四项要求之译文。

1. 公司之长期雇员，非有充分理由，不得予以解雇。
2. 被解雇之三十四名雇员应予复职；在中日战事爆发后被解雇之雇员，应有权申请重新受雇。
3. 若公司因业务清淡拟解雇雇员，应实行轮班制度，但每名雇员在每二十八天内应至少获得十八天工作（夜班不计在内）。因工作清淡而被解雇之雇员，应按其受雇年限，每满一年发给一个月薪金作为奖金。
4. 雇员每年应享有至少八天带薪假期。若雇员在假期内继续工作，应发给双倍工资。自中日战事爆发以来之假期，亦应照付工资。
5. 每逢中国新年，每名雇员应发给相当于两周薪金的奖金。
6. 雇员在受雇期间受伤，公司应负责支付医疗及住院费用。若雇员

page_data.en:
permanently disabled during the course of employment, he
should be given a grant of $400 cash. If the employee
is fatally injured during the course of employment, the
Company will give his family a grant of $500 cash.
7. When an employee dies, or cannot work any further owing to
ill-health, the Company will pay him, or his family, the
following grant:-
(a) No grant to be made for less than five years
employment.
(b) Employees with over five and less than twenty
years service, a grant of $200 to $300 cash.
(c) Employees with over twenty and less than thirty
years service, a grant of $320 to $450 cash.
8. Apprentices who have served a five years apprenticeship,
are to be considered and paid as qualified tradesmen.
9. In future deductions will not be made from employees' wages
in connection with any case of theft occurring in the firm.
Moneys deducted in connection with the theft of lead last
Winter to be refunded.
10. Permanent employees to be granted a bonus of $2.00 per week,
owing to the present high cost of rice. This bonus to be
paid even if a full week has not been worked.
11. Employees living in the part of Settlement, south of the
Soochow Creek or in the French Concession, to be granted
free transportation to and from their employment, on board
the Company's launches.
page_data.zh:
若在受雇期间永久残疾，应发给其400元现金补助。若雇员在受雇期间因伤致死，公司将向其家属发放500元现金补助。

7. 当雇员死亡，或因健康原因无法继续工作时，公司将向其本人或其家属支付下列补助：-
(a) 受雇不满五年者，不予发放补助。
(b) 受雇超过五年但不足二十年者，发放现金补助200至300元。
(c) 受雇超过二十年但不足三十年者，发放现金补助320至450元。

8. 已完成五年学徒期的学徒，应视为合格技工并按此待遇支付薪酬。

9. 今后，不得因公司内发生的任何盗窃案件而从雇员工资中扣款。去年冬季因铅材失窃案所扣除的款项应予退还。

10. 鉴于目前米价高昂，向长期雇员每周发放2.00元奖金。即使未满一周工作时间，亦应支付此奖金。

11. 居住在苏州河以南公共租界区域或法租界的雇员，由公司交通艇免费接送往返工作地点。

page_data.en:
12. Employees to be paid their wages during the time of the
strike.
13. The arrested employee, named Chang Tun Sung ( 張得勝 ),
to be released, before the demands are considered.
14. Employees in the Pump Room will be considered as permanent
workers.

(Signed) The Representatives.
page_data.zh:
12. 罢工期间，雇员应照常领取工资。
13. 在审议各项要求之前，须释放被捕雇员张得胜（Chang Tun Sung）。
14. 泵房雇员将被视为正式工人。

（签名）代表们

3rd. REPORT
Date Nov. 23rd. 19 39.
Subject Strike at the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtzepoo Road.
Made by D.S.I. Ross. Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Sir,

During the course of the day it was learned that the management of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., on making a check of the workers, discovered that some further five hundred Painters, Carpenters and Masons etc. had failed to report for work at 7 a.m. 23-11-39, making a total of approximately 1,500 absentees. Mr. L. Beattie (Superintendent) when interviewed, stated that he had received certain information that at 6.30 a.m. 23-11-39 an unknown coolie wearing a Chinese Workers Welfare Association Badge entered the Docks, and intimidated several of the boiler-makers, also that a letter had been received by the Launch Lodah's threatening them with violence should they still remain loyal to the Company. A translated copy of the letter is attached.

It has been ascertained that the management have engaged thirty-five Russian employees in place of some of those on strike, and that they intend to post a notice urging all other workers to return to work. A translation of which is hereto attached.

Mr. Beattie further stated that commencing from 6 a.m. 24-11-39 the management had decided to run two launches from the Customs Jetty to the works, to enable workers who wished to continue work do so.

It was observed that between the hours of 6 a.m. and 8 a.m. 23-11-39 two members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party were posted on sentry duty at the main entrance to the Docks. It is believed that these guards will be maintained for the duration of the strike.

报告人：副巡官罗斯 (D.S.I. Ross)。由 **〔此处转录不清〕** 转呈

先生：

日间获悉，上海船坞有限公司管理层在点名核查工人时，发现另有约五百名油漆工、木工和泥瓦匠等未于 1939 年 11 月 23 日上午 7 时到岗上班，致使缺勤总人数达到约 1,500 人。 superintendent（总监） L. Beattie 先生在接受问询时表示，他收到某些情报称，1939 年 11 月 23 日上午 6 时 30 分，一名佩戴“中国工人福利会”徽章的未知苦力进入船坞，恐吓了几名锅炉工；此外，“洛达”号 (Launch Lodah) 小轮收到一封信件，威胁若其继续效忠公司，将对其施以暴力。该信件的译本附后。

经查实，管理层已雇佣三十五名俄籍雇员，以替代部分罢工人员，并打算张贴告示，敦促其他所有工人返岗复工。告示译文亦附后。

Beattie 先生进一步表示，自 1939 年 11 月 24 日上午 6 时起，管理层决定从海关码头开行两班小轮前往厂区，以便希望继续工作的工人能够到岗。

观察发现，1939 年 11 月 23 日上午 6 时至 8 时期间，两名日本海军陆战队队员在船坞主入口处站岗执勤。据信，这些警卫将在罢工持续期间一直驻守。

Translation of Notice to be posted by the
Management of the Shanghai Dockyard's Ltd.

In connection with the unauthorized stoppage of work
in this yard yesterday, the Company hereby strongly advise
all workmen to return to duty without further loss of time
and wages, because no stopping from work will have even
the smallest benefit for the discharged coolie from the
Company.

Because so many untrue stories are being spread about,
the Company hereby make it clear that these coolie workmen
have been discharged only in accordance with the Company's
regular policy, and under exactly the same conditions of
pay and compensation as their fellow coolies recently in
Company's Pootung Yard. Their wages and compensation are and
have been ready for payment since Saturday, but some of the
coolies have foolishly made trouble over the matter, have
seriously damaged the Company's property and behaved like
children. Therefore, the Company is sure that all loyal
workmen will not listen further to the trouble makers, but
return to duty without delay and so keep up the good
friendship between the workmen and the Company.
page_data.zh:
上海船坞有限公司管理层张贴告示之译文

鉴于昨日本船坞发生未经授权的停工事件，本公司特此强烈劝告所有工人立即返岗复工，以免进一步损失工时与工资，因为停工对于被本公司解雇的苦力而言，绝无丝毫益处。

由于目前流传着诸多不实谣言，本公司特此澄清：这些苦力工人的解雇仅系依照本公司之常规政策执行，其薪资与补偿条件与近期在本公司浦东船坞工作的其他苦力完全相同。他们的工资及补偿款自上周六起即已备妥待付，但部分苦力却愚昧地就此滋事，严重损坏了公司财产，行为如同孩童般幼稚。因此，本公司确信所有忠诚的工人将不再听信煽动者之言，而是立即返岗复工，从而维持工人与公司之间的良好友好关系。

Translation of a Letter Addressed by
Strikers to Launch Laodah's of the
Shanghai Dockyard's Ltd..

Not dated.

To the Launch Laodahs,

This letter is being addressed to you owing to the
Factory pressing the innocent, discharged workmen, and
all workmen are not satisfied, so they have acted. It
is hoped the various Laodahs, to assist each other, will
stop running the launches temporarily, on account of
brotherhood and to recover the welfare of the workmen.

This is only a letter of advice at present. If you
do not awake, there will probably be ordure. It will then
be too late to repent. This is a reminder.

Mud hopper and
Sheerlegs the same

(Signed) By this association.

Envelope printed: CHINESE WORKERS WELFARE ASSOCIATION,
EASTERN BRANCH SHANGHAI.

无日期。

致各位驳船老大：

鉴于厂方压迫无辜的被解雇工人，全体工人都感到不满，因此采取了行动。希望各位老大出于兄弟情谊，并为了恢复工人的福利，能互相协助，暂时停止运营驳船。

目前这只是一封劝告信。如果你们不觉醒，恐怕会发生污秽之事（注：原文为 ordure，意指肮脏或令人不悦的后果）。届时后悔就太晚了。特此提醒。

泥驳和起重船同样适用

（签名）本会

Sir:
On the 18-11-1939, the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640
Yangtzepoo Road, dismissed thirty-four employees, whose
services the company considered to be undesirable.
Following their dismissal, the employees registered
with the Japanese sponsored Chinese Workers Welfare Associa-
tion. Following their application to the officials of the
Association that they should mediate in the trouble, the
workers were assured by the Chairman, Moh Ling Tsong( 莫林
章 ), that he himself would contact the management, and
arrange a settlement of the dispute.
At 6.54 a.m. 22-11-1939, a telephone call was received
from Mr. L. Beattie, Superintendent of the Shanghai Dockyards
Ltd., to the effect that the dismissed employees were prevent-
ing the other workers from entering the Docks.
In response to this message, a party of Police attended,
and upon making enquiries were informed by the dismissed
workers that they thought their dismissal to be unfair, and
they wished to persuade the remainder of the employees of the
firm to strike in sympathy.
In all some three hundred workers were congregated on
Yangtzepoo Road, outside the Dock entrance of the company,
at 516, Yangtzepoo Road. Amongst the crowd was seen a number
of the dismissed employees, and it was observed that a large
number of the workers were wearing Union badges issued by the
Chinese Workers Welfare Association.
Mr. Beattie was informed regarding the assertions of
wrongful dismissal, and at his request the Police informed
the dismissed employees that if they selected three or four
representives to visit the office at 10 a.m., the management

先生：

1939年11月18日，位于杨树浦路640号的上海船坞有限公司解雇了三十四名雇员，公司认为这些人的表现不佳。

被解雇后，这些雇员在日方支持的“中国工人福利会”进行了登记。在他们向该会官员申请调解纠纷后，该会主席莫林章（Moh Ling Tsong）向工人们保证，他将亲自与管理层联系，并安排解决此争端。

1939年11月22日上午6时54分，上海船坞有限公司主管L. Beattie先生打来电话，称被解雇的雇员正在阻止其他工人进入船坞。

接到此消息后，一队警员前往现场。经询问，被解雇的工人告知警员，他们认为解雇是不公正的，并希望说服该公司的其余雇员举行同情罢工。

总计约有三百名工人聚集在杨树浦路516号该公司船坞入口外的杨树浦路上。人群中可见多名被解雇的雇员，并且观察到大量工人佩戴着由中国工人福利会颁发的工会徽章。

警方将有关不当解雇的说法告知了Beattie先生，应其要求，警方通知被解雇的雇员，如果他们选出三至四名代表于上午10时前往办公室，管理层

resulted in the above three named coolies, leading an attack

buckets, and wooden stools, which they picked up from nearby
shops.

the offices of the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640, Yangtszepoo
Road, an employee named Hou Shu Zei(賀守財), Coolie, No. 134,
blew a Police whistle, and incited the workers to throw stones
at the office windows, which resulted in numerous panes of
glass being broken, but no injuries were sustained by the office
staff.

    A check of the workers revealed that some 300 of the
Permanent Staff had already commenced work. Almost 700 workers
had failed to start. The contract workers were present as usual.
At the tiffin hour interval, the above mentioned 300 workers
left the premises and failed to return.
    Demands have not as yet been presented to the management,
and the attitude of the latter appears to be that they will
not re-engage the dismissed employees under any circumstances,
and should other workers become members of the Chinese Workers
Welfare Association, they will be instantly dismissed.
    On the 17-11-1939, literature of a pro-Japanese nature
urging the workers to become members of the Chinese Workers
Welfare Association was distributed at the Works. At an early
hour this morning, some unknown persons pasted a poster on the
wall of the Works, which urged the employees to strike in
sympathy with the dismissed workers. A translation of this is
attached hereto.
    Detectives are now making efforts to trace the ringleaders
in the strike.
    A strong party of Police has been posted on duty at the
premises.
    The D.O. "D" Division was informed, and attended the scene."
    Reserves of police were summoned from the Reserve Unit (
East), and attended the scene.

page_data.en:
Translation of a Poster found outside
the Shanghai Dockyards Ltd., 640 Yangtszepoo Road.

Through the diligent work of the faithful employees, the
Shanghai Dockyards has been developed into a great concern. The
management, instead of remunerating them, has dismissed some of
the workers, regardless of their long service, ranging from 10
to 40 years. We spent our youth in the service of the company,
and now when we have become aged, we are dismissed. Where can
we find jobs, especially at the present time, when the cost of
living has greatly increased. How can we support our families?
We are unable to solve the trouble and, therefore, request the
rest of the workers to render us some assistance. You are also
liable to be dismissed in the same manner. Please don't work
until the management promises to reinstate the dismissed workers.
Recognise the Union and the rights of the representatives of the
workers, and also have the management provide a guarantee that
in future no workers will be dismissed without any reason.

J. J. Ross
22/7/39

在上海杨树浦路640号上海船坞有限公司（Shanghai Dockyards Ltd.）外发现的一张传单的译文。

通过忠诚员工的勤勉工作，上海船坞已发展成为一家大型企业。管理层非但没有给予他们应有的报酬，反而解雇了一些工人，全然不顾他们长达10至40年的长期服务。我们将青春奉献给了公司，如今当我们年老时，却遭到解雇。在当下生活费用大幅上涨的时期，我们何处才能找到工作？我们又如何养家糊口？我们无法自行解决这一困境，因此请求其余工人向我们提供援助。你们同样可能以同样的方式被解雇。在管理层承诺复职被解雇工人之前，请勿开工。承认工会及工人代表的权利，并要求管理层提供保证，今后不得无故解雇任何工人。

J. J. Ross
1939年7月22日

Manifesto issued by the Chinese Workers' Welfare Association
to labourers.

Since the outbreak of the 1937 hostilities, millions of
labourers have been rendered unemployed, and have become
so poor that they cannot support themselves and their
families, as if they have been put in hell. This is
entirely caused by communism in our country, as we Chinese
people have never suffered from the present agony since the
establishment of Taoism by Confucius.

The object of our association is:-

(1) To unite all the labourers, render mutual assistance,
eliminate the Communist Party, and seek the welfare
for the workers, so that we can spend our lives
happily.

(2) To improve the friendship with the neighbouring
country of the same race and literature, so as to
establish the foundation of peace in the Orient.

Dear labourers, make your mind to go along the road
to glory. Don't deviate.

Chinese Workers' Welfare
Association.
page_data.zh:
中国工人福利协会向劳工发布的宣言。

自1937年战事爆发以来，数百万劳工失业，陷入贫困，无法维持自身及家人的生计，犹如身处地狱。这完全是由我国共产主义所致，自从孔子创立道教以来，我们中国人从未遭受过如今的痛苦。

本协会的宗旨是：

(1) 团结所有劳工，互助合作，铲除共产党，谋求工人福利，使我们能够幸福地度过一生。

(2) 增进与同文同种的邻邦的友谊，以奠定东方和平的基础。

亲爱的劳工们，决心走上光荣之路。不要偏离。

中国工人福利协会

This Association has been brought into beinz for the 
promotion of the welfare of the Chinese labourers 

who have been led astray in the past by the propaganda 
of the Three Peoples' Principles. 

Technical skill being the weapon of the workers, 
therefore we must devote our attention and efforts 
towards the improvement of technical efficiency in 
order to lay a good foundation for the reconstruction 
of a new China. 

The labourers must help one another in order to 
ensure unity. 

For the purpose of checking the tendency of expansion 
of the European and American influence in Fast Agia, 
we must direct sur endeavours towards the early 
termimition of the disastrous hostilities and the 
realization of a Sino-Japanese rapproahement. 

The aims and objects of this Association mfve been 
given in the foregoing. Since its inauguration in 
last autumn, the number of individual members who 
have registered with the Association, is now over 
100,000. A total of over 70 labour unions have 
joined the Association. It is very significant to 
note that the majority of the members of the 
Association are in the Internatioml Settlement south 
of the Soochow Creek and the French Concession. 

In return for the favour and support given by those 
concerned, the Association is planning the establish- 
ment of medical services, employment bureaux, legal 


advice services, the teaching of Japanese language

and for the salvation of themselves.

Preparatory Committee of the Chinese LAabourers' 

Welfare Association 

Due to the decadence of Chinese morals and the 
degeneration of other Oriental virtues, the people of 

Cathay have, during recent years, been exposed to the 

wide spread influence of Communist doctrines, which, 

until the outbreak of the current hostilities, had taken 
an especially strong hold of millions of the Chinese 
labour population. The deplorable consequences are, 

as we witness to-day, the ruination of homes, and the 

unemployment of several millions of workers. whose 

present condition is indeed comparable to the so-called 
hell-on-earth. Since urgency of the situation demands 

an immediate improvement, for the good of all concerned, 
we have secured the approval and support of wealthy and 
influential circles for the organization of the "Chinese 

Labourers' Welfare Association," The association.aims at 

increased technical efficiency in industry, the improve- 

ment of living conditions of workers, relief for the 
unemployed, and the establiahment of cooperatives for 
the benefit of workers. In proceeding with our task, 

we are guided by the two principles given hereunder : 

(1) Internally, to revive ancient Chinese morals and to 
banish communist influences for the uplift of Chinese 
industrial circles. 

(2) Externally, to maintain friendly relations with our 
neighbour country in order to contribute our efforts 
towards the establishment of lnating peace in East 
Asia. 

Fellow compatriots who are in the field of industry, 
let us be firm in our determination and march towards our 


ultimate goal.
